nodes.name: Image of the double transfer in stable homotopy
nodes.statement: The double $S^1$-transfer is a stable morphism $\mathrm{tr}_2 : \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty _+ \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_+ \rightarrow S^{-2}$; determining its image in stable homotopy groups is a fundamental problem.
nodes.statement_short: Determine the image of the double $S^1$-transfer $\mathrm{tr}_2$ in the stable homotopy groups.

nodes.name: Induced module morphism $\tilde{f}$
nodes.statement: If $E$ is a ring spectrum and $M$ is an $E$-module the morphism of $E$-module spectra induced by a morphism of spectra $f : X \rightarrow M$ is denoted $\tilde{f} : E \wedge X \rightarrow M$.

nodes.name: Topological generator $\gamma$
nodes.statement: Let $\gamma \in \mathbb{Z}$ be a topological generator of the $p$-adic units $\mathbb{Z}_p^\times$.

nodes.name: Non-connective image of J theory Ad
nodes.statement: Non-connective image of $J$ theory, ${Ad}$, is defined by the cofibre sequence \[ {Ad} \rightarrow KU_{(p)} \stackrel{\psi^\gamma -1} {\rightarrow} KU_{(p)} \rightarrow , \] where $\psi^\gamma$ is the stable Adams operation, which is a morphism of ring spectra.
nodes.statement_short: $Ad$ is the fibre of $\psi^\gamma-1$ on $KU_{(p)}$.

nodes.name: Independence of Ad from the choice of gamma
nodes.statement: The homotopy type of ${Ad}$ is independent of the choice of $\gamma$ (cf. \cite{knapp}).
conclusions: The homotopy type of ${Ad}$ is independent of the choice of $\gamma$

nodes.name: Ad modulo p-infinity is L_1 S/p-infinity
nodes.statement: The spectrum ${Ad}$ is a $KU$-module spectrum, in particular is $KU$-local; moreover, there are equivalences \[ {Ad} / p^\infty \simeq {Ad} \wedge S/p^\infty \simeq (L_1 S) \wedge S/p^\infty \simeq L_1 (S/p^\infty) \] (cf. \cite[Lemma 8.7]{ravenel}), where $L_ 1$ is Bousfield localization with respect to $p$-local $K$-theory.
nodes.statement_short: $Ad$ is $KU$-local and $Ad/p^\infty \simeq L_1(S/p^\infty)$.

nodes.name: Commutative diagram for maps to L_1 S/p-infinity
nodes.statement: Hence there is a commutative diagram \begin{eqnarray} \xymatrix{ && L_1 S/p^\infty \ar[d]^\alpha \\ KU_{(p)} \ar[r] & KU _{\mathbb{Q}} \ar[r]^q \ar[d]_{\psi^\gamma -1} & KU /p^\infty \ar[d]^{\psi^\gamma - 1} \\ & KU_{\mathbb{Q}} \ar[r] & KU /p^\infty } \end{eqnarray} in which the three-term vertical and horizontal sequences are cofibre sequences and $q$ is the reduction morphism.
nodes.statement_short: $L_1S/p^\infty$ maps via $\alpha$ to $KU/p^\infty$, compatibly with $\psi^\gamma-1$ and the reduction $q$.

nodes.name: Ad cofibre sequence diagram (1)
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ && L_1 S/p^\infty \ar[d]^\alpha \\ KU_{(p)} \ar[r] & KU _{\mathbb{Q}} \ar[r]^q \ar[d]_{\psi^\gamma -1} & KU /p^\infty \ar[d]^{\psi^\gamma - 1} \\ & KU_{\mathbb{Q}} \ar[r] & KU /p^\infty }
nodes.label: eqn:Ad_cofibre_seq

nodes.name: Q-representative
nodes.statement: A $\mathbb{Q}$-representative of a morphism of spectra $g : Y \rightarrow L_1 S /p^\infty$ is a morphism $f : Y \rightarrow KU_{\mathbb{Q}}$ which makes the following diagram commute \begin{eqnarray} \xymatrix{ Y \ar[r]^g \ar[d]_f & L_1 S /p^\infty \ar[d]^\alpha \\ KU_{\mathbb{Q}} \ar[r]_q & KU/p^\infty. } \end{eqnarray}
differentia: which makes the following diagram commute

nodes.name: Q-representative square (2)
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ Y \ar[r]^g \ar[d]_f & L_1 S /p^\infty \ar[d]^\alpha \\ KU_{\mathbb{Q}} \ar[r]_q & KU/p^\infty. }
nodes.label: eqn:KU-commutative-ad

nodes.name: Integrality of (psi^gamma - 1) f
nodes.statement: If $f$ is a $\mathbb{Q}$-representative of $g$, then $(\psi^\gamma -1) f$ lies in the image of $KU^0_{(p)}Y \rightarrow KU^0_{\mathbb{Q}} Y$.
assumptions: $f$ is a $\mathbb{Q}$-representative of $g$
conclusions: $(\psi^\gamma -1) f$ lies in the image of $KU^0_{(p)}Y \rightarrow KU^0_{\mathbb{Q}} Y$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement: Follows from the commutativity of the square in diagram (\ref{eqn:Ad_cofibre_seq}).
nodes.statement_short: Read off from the commuting square of diagram (1).

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of Q-representatives
nodes.statement: Let $Y$ be a spectrum such that $KU ^*_{(p)} Y$ is a finitely-generated free $KU_{(p)*}$-module and $KU^{\mathrm{odd}}_{(p)}Y=0$. Then \begin{enumerate} \item the morphism $[Y, L_1 S /p^\infty ] \rightarrow [Y, KU/p^\infty]$ is injective; \item any morphism $g : Y \rightarrow L_1 S /p^\infty$ admits a $\mathbb{Q}$-representative; \item a morphism $f: Y \rightarrow KU_{\mathbb{Q}}$ such that $(\psi^\gamma -1) f$ lies in the image of $KU^0_{(p)}Y \rightarrow KU^0_{\mathbb{Q}} Y$ is the $\mathbb{Q}$-representative of a unique morphism $g : Y \rightarrow L_1 S/p^\infty$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: For $Y$ with free, even $p$-local $KU$-cohomology, maps to $L_1S/p^\infty$ are detected in $KU/p^\infty$ and correspond to $\mathbb{Q}$-representatives.
assumptions: $Y$ be a spectrum such that $KU ^*_{(p)} Y$ is a finitely-generated free $KU_{(p)*}$-module and $KU^{\mathrm{odd}}_{(p)}Y=0$
conclusions: the morphism $[Y, L_1 S /p^\infty ] \rightarrow [Y, KU/p^\infty]$ is injective
any morphism $g : Y \rightarrow L_1 S /p^\infty$ admits a $\mathbb{Q}$-representative

a morphism $f: Y \rightarrow KU_{\mathbb{Q}}$ such that $(\psi^\gamma -1) f$ lies in the image of $KU^0_{(p)}Y \rightarrow KU^0_{\mathbb{Q}} Y$ is the $\mathbb{Q}$-representative of a unique morphism $g : Y \rightarrow L_1 S/p^\infty$
nodes.label: prop:represent-ad

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.3
nodes.statement: Straightforward.
nodes.statement_short: Asserted to be straightforward.

nodes.name: Thom spectra over CP^n satisfy the hypotheses
nodes.statement: The hypotheses of Proposition \ref{prop:represent-ad} are satisfied for $Y$ the Thom spectrum of a finite rank virtual $\mathbb{C}$-vector bundle over $\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^n$ and for smash products of spectra of this type.

nodes.name: Landweber exact ring spectrum
nodes.statement: Recall that a complex oriented ring spectrum $E$ is Landweber exact if the orientation $MU_* \rightarrow E_*$ is Landweber exact for the Hopf algebroid $(MU_* , MU_*MU)$ (see Definition \ref{def:Landweber_exact}).
differentia: the orientation $MU_* \rightarrow E_*$ is Landweber exact for the Hopf algebroid $(MU_* , MU_*MU)$

nodes.name: Comodule morphisms into MU_*E for Landweber exact E
nodes.statement: Let $E$ be a Landweber exact complex oriented ring spectrum and $Y$ be a spectrum. \begin{enumerate} \item There exist natural isomorphisms \[ \mathrm{Hom}_{MU_* MU} (MU_* Y, MU_* E) \cong \mathrm{Hom}_{MU_*} (MU_* Y , E_*) \cong \mathrm{Hom}_{E_*} (E_* Y, E_*). \] \item For a morphism of spectra $f : Y \rightarrow E$, the comodule morphism $MU_* f : MU_* Y \rightarrow MU_* E$ corresponds via the above isomorphisms to the morphism of $E_*$-modules $\tilde{f}_* : E_* Y \rightarrow E_*$ induced by $ \tilde{f}: E \wedge Y \rightarrow E$. \end{enumerate}
assumptions: $E$ be a Landweber exact complex oriented ring spectrum and $Y$ be a spectrum
conclusions: There exist natural isomorphisms \[ \mathrm{Hom}_{MU_* MU} (MU_* Y, MU_* E) \cong \mathrm{Hom}_{MU_*} (MU_* Y , E_*) \cong \mathrm{Hom}_{E_*} (E_* Y, E_*).

For a morphism of spectra $f : Y \rightarrow E$, the comodule morphism $MU_* f : MU_* Y \rightarrow MU_* E$ corresponds via the above isomorphisms to the morphism of $E_*$-modules $\tilde{f}_* : E_* Y \rightarrow E_*$ induced by $ \tilde{f}: E \wedge Y \rightarrow E$
nodes.label: lem:Landweber_exact

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.5
nodes.statement: The first isomorphism of part (1) follows from the identification of $MU_*E$ as the extended comodule $MU_*MU \otimes_{MU_*} E_*$ and the second from the isomorphism of $E_*$-modules $E_* Y \cong E_* \otimes_{MU_*} MU_* Y$ which is a consequence of Landweber exactness. The final statement is straightforward.
nodes.statement_short: Extended-comodule identification of $MU_*E$ plus the Landweber-exact isomorphism $E_*Y\cong E_*\otimes MU_*Y$.

nodes.name: Hattori-Stong monomorphism for Landweber exact theories
nodes.statement: Let $E$ be a Landweber exact complex oriented ring spectrum, then the morphism $L_1 S /p^\infty \rightarrow KU/p^\infty$ induces a monomorphism of $E_* E$-comodules, $E_* /p^\infty [v_1^{-1}] \hookrightarrow E_* KU /p^\infty$.
assumptions: $E$ be a Landweber exact complex oriented ring spectrum
conclusions: the morphism $L_1 S /p^\infty \rightarrow KU/p^\infty$ induces a monomorphism of $E_* E$-comodules, $E_* /p^\infty [v_1^{-1}] \hookrightarrow E_* KU /p^\infty$
nodes.label: lem:hattori-stong

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.6
nodes.statement: By Landweber exactness, it suffices to prove this result for the universal case $E=MU$, where it is a consequence of the Hattori-Stong theorem (cf. \cite[Proposition 20.33]{switzer}), which states that the $KU$-Hurewicz morphism $MU_* \rightarrow MU_*KU$ is rationally faithful (in the terminology of \cite[Definition 1.1]{laures}), which is equivalent to the statement that $MU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}/ \mathbb{Z} \hookrightarrow MU_* KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}/ \mathbb{Z}$ is a monomorphism. Hence, on the $p$-local component, this gives a monomorphism of $MU_*MU$-comodules $MU_* /p^\infty \hookrightarrow MU_* KU /p^\infty$. The morphism of $MU_*MU$-comodules $MU_* /p^\infty [v_1^{-1}] \rightarrow MU_* KU/p^\infty$ corresponds to the localization of the above morphism, inverting $v_1$, since the morphism $L_1 S \rightarrow KU_{(p)}$ factors the unit $S \rightarrow KU_{(p)}$. The result follows.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $E=MU$ by Landweber exactness, apply the Hattori-Stong theorem, then invert $v_1$.

nodes.name: Reduce to MU and apply Hattori-Stong
nodes.statement: By Landweber exactness, it suffices to prove this result for the universal case $E=MU$, where it is a consequence of the Hattori-Stong theorem (cf. \cite[Proposition 20.33]{switzer}), which states that the $KU$-Hurewicz morphism $MU_* \rightarrow MU_*KU$ is rationally faithful (in the terminology of \cite[Definition 1.1]{laures}), which is equivalent to the statement that $MU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}/ \mathbb{Z} \hookrightarrow MU_* KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}/ \mathbb{Z}$ is a monomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $E=MU$, where the Hattori-Stong theorem gives rational faithfulness.

nodes.name: p-local monomorphism
nodes.statement: Hence, on the $p$-local component, this gives a monomorphism of $MU_*MU$-comodules $MU_* /p^\infty \hookrightarrow MU_* KU /p^\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Pass to the $p$-local component.

nodes.name: Invert v_1
nodes.statement: The morphism of $MU_*MU$-comodules $MU_* /p^\infty [v_1^{-1}] \rightarrow MU_* KU/p^\infty$ corresponds to the localization of the above morphism, inverting $v_1$, since the morphism $L_1 S \rightarrow KU_{(p)}$ factors the unit $S \rightarrow KU_{(p)}$. The result follows.
nodes.statement_short: Localize by inverting $v_1$.

nodes.name: E-homology of a map to L_1 S/p-infinity via its Q-representative
nodes.statement: Let $E$ be a Landweber exact complex oriented ring spectrum and $g: Y \rightarrow L_1 S /p^\infty$ be a morphism of spectra which admits a $\mathbb{Q}$-representative $f: Y \rightarrow KU_{\mathbb{Q}}$. Then \begin{enumerate} \item the morphism $E_* (g) : E_* Y \rightarrow E_* (L_1 S /p^\infty)$ is determined by $E_* (f)$ via the commutative diagram of morphisms of $E_*E$-comodules: \[ \xymatrix{ E_* Y \ar[r]^{E_* (g)} \ar[d]_{E_*(f)} & E_*/p^\infty [v_1^{-1}] \ar@{^(->}[d] \\ E_* KU \otimes \mathbb{Q} \ar@{->>}[r] & E_* KU/p^\infty . } \] \item The morphism $E_* (f)$ is determined by the morphism of $KU_*$-modules $\tilde{f}_* : KU_* Y \rightarrow KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ induced by $f$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: For Landweber exact $E$, $E_*(g)$ is determined by $E_*(f)$, which is determined by $\tilde f_*$ on $KU$-homology.
assumptions: $E$ be a Landweber exact complex oriented ring spectrum and
$g: Y \rightarrow L_1 S /p^\infty$ be a morphism of spectra which admits a $\mathbb{Q}$-representative $f: Y \rightarrow KU_{\mathbb{Q}}$
conclusions: the morphism $E_* (g) : E_* Y \rightarrow E_* (L_1 S /p^\infty)$ is determined by $E_* (f)$ via the commutative diagram of morphisms of $E_*E$-comodules: \[ \xymatrix{ E_* Y \ar[r]^{E_* (g)} \ar[d]_{E_*(f)} & E_*/p^\infty [v_1^{-1}] \ar@{^(->}[d] \\ E_* KU \otimes \mathbb{Q} \ar@{->>}[r] & E_* KU/p^\infty . } \]
The morphism $E_* (f)$ is determined by the morphism of $KU_*$-modules $\tilde{f}_* : KU_* Y \rightarrow KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ induced by $f$
nodes.label: prop:f,g-Landweber

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.7
nodes.statement: Again, by Landweber exactness, it is sufficient to prove the result for the universal case, $E = MU$. The commutative diagram (\ref{eqn:KU-commutative-ad}) induces a commutative diagram of $MU_* MU$-comodules: \[ \xymatrix{ MU_* Y \ar[r]^{MU_* (g)} \ar@{^(->}[d]_{MU_*(f)} & MU_* /p^\infty [v_1 ^{-1}] \ar@{^(->}[d] \\ MU_*KU \otimes \mathbb{Q} \ar@{->>}[r] & MU_* KU /p^\infty, } \] in which $MU_* /p^\infty [v_1^{-1}] \rightarrow MU_* KU /p^\infty$ is injective, by the Hattori-Stong theorem (Lemma \ref{lem:hattori-stong}), and $MU_* KU \otimes \mathbb{Q} \rightarrow MU_* KU /p^\infty$ is the canonical surjection. Thus, $MU_* (g)$ is determined by the total composite of the diagram, hence by the morphism of $MU_*MU$-comodules $MU_* Y \stackrel{MU_* (f)}{\rightarrow}MU_* KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}$. The final statement follows from Lemma \ref{lem:Landweber_exact}, which implies that the morphism $MU_*(f)$ is the composite \[ MU_* Y \stackrel{\psi}{\rightarrow} MU_* MU \otimes _{MU_*} MU_* Y \rightarrow MU_*MU \otimes _{MU_*} KU_* Y \stackrel{MU_* MU \otimes \tilde{f}_*}{\rightarrow} MU_*KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}, \] where $\psi$ is the comodule structure morphism and the second morphism is induced by $MU_* Y \rightarrow KU_* Y$, given by the orientation of $KU$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $E=MU$; the Hattori-Stong injection makes $MU_*(g)$ determined by $MU_*(f)$, which Lemma 2.5 expresses via $\tilde f_*$.

nodes.name: Reduce to MU
nodes.statement: Again, by Landweber exactness, it is sufficient to prove the result for the universal case, $E = MU$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the universal case $E=MU$.

nodes.name: Part (1)
nodes.statement: The commutative diagram (\ref{eqn:KU-commutative-ad}) induces a commutative diagram of $MU_* MU$-comodules: \[ \xymatrix{ MU_* Y \ar[r]^{MU_* (g)} \ar@{^(->}[d]_{MU_*(f)} & MU_* /p^\infty [v_1 ^{-1}] \ar@{^(->}[d] \\ MU_*KU \otimes \mathbb{Q} \ar@{->>}[r] & MU_* KU /p^\infty, } \] in which $MU_* /p^\infty [v_1^{-1}] \rightarrow MU_* KU /p^\infty$ is injective, by the Hattori-Stong theorem (Lemma \ref{lem:hattori-stong}), and $MU_* KU \otimes \mathbb{Q} \rightarrow MU_* KU /p^\infty$ is the canonical surjection. Thus, $MU_* (g)$ is determined by the total composite of the diagram, hence by the morphism of $MU_*MU$-comodules $MU_* Y \stackrel{MU_* (f)}{\rightarrow}MU_* KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}$.
nodes.statement_short: Diagram (2) and the Hattori-Stong injection determine $MU_*(g)$ by $MU_*(f)$.

nodes.name: Part (2)
nodes.statement: The final statement follows from Lemma \ref{lem:Landweber_exact}, which implies that the morphism $MU_*(f)$ is the composite \[ MU_* Y \stackrel{\psi}{\rightarrow} MU_* MU \otimes _{MU_*} MU_* Y \rightarrow MU_*MU \otimes _{MU_*} KU_* Y \stackrel{MU_* MU \otimes \tilde{f}_*}{\rightarrow} MU_*KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}, \] where $\psi$ is the comodule structure morphism and the second morphism is induced by $MU_* Y \rightarrow KU_* Y$, given by the orientation of $KU$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 2.5 writes $MU_*(f)$ via $\tilde f_*$.

nodes.name: KU-homology factorization of a map to L_1 S/p-infinity
nodes.statement: Let $g: Y \rightarrow L_1 S /p^\infty$ be a morphism of spectra which admits a $\mathbb{Q}$-representative $f: Y \rightarrow KU_{\mathbb{Q}}$. Then there is an induced commutative diagram of morphisms of $KU_*$-modules: \[ \xymatrix{ KU_* Y \ar[r]^{KU_* (g)} \ar[d]^{KU_* (f)} \ar @{-->}@/_3pc/[dd]_{\tilde{f}_*} & KU_*/p^\infty \ar[d] \ar@/^3pc/[dd]^{KU_* /p^\infty} \\ KU_*KU \otimes \mathbb{Q} \ar[r] \ar@{-->}[d] & KU_* KU/p^\infty \ar@{-->}[d] \\ KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} \ar@{->>}[r] & KU_*/p^\infty } \] in which the solid arrows are morphisms of $KU_*KU$-comodules and the lower vertical morphisms are induced by the augmentation $KU_* KU \rightarrow KU_*$. In particular, the comodule morphism $KU_* (g) : KU_* Y \rightarrow KU_* /p^\infty$ factorizes as morphisms of $KU_*$-modules as \[ KU_ * Y \stackrel{\tilde{f}_*} {\rightarrow} KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} \twoheadrightarrow KU_* /p^\infty. \]
nodes.statement_short: $KU_*(g)$ factors as $\tilde f_*$ followed by $KU_*\otimes\mathbb{Q}\twoheadrightarrow KU_*/p^\infty$.
assumptions: $g: Y \rightarrow L_1 S /p^\infty$ be a morphism of spectra which admits a $\mathbb{Q}$-representative $f: Y \rightarrow KU_{\mathbb{Q}}$
conclusions: there is an induced commutative diagram of morphisms of $KU_*$-modules: \[ \xymatrix{ KU_* Y \ar[r]^{KU_* (g)} \ar[d]^{KU_* (f)} \ar @{-->}@/_3pc/[dd]_{\tilde{f}_*} & KU_*/p^\infty \ar[d] \ar@/^3pc/[dd]^{KU_* /p^\infty} \\ KU_*KU \otimes \mathbb{Q} \ar[r] \ar@{-->}[d] & KU_* KU/p^\infty \ar@{-->}[d] \\ KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} \ar@{->>}[r] & KU_*/p^\infty } \] in which the solid arrows are morphisms of $KU_*KU$-comodules and the lower vertical morphisms are induced by the augmentation $KU_* KU \rightarrow KU_*$

nodes.name: MU Hopf algebroid is the Lazard Hopf algebroid (L, LB)
nodes.statement: To fix notation, recall that the Hopf algebroid $(MU_* , MU_*MU)$ is isomorphic to the Hopf algebroid $(L, LB)$ which represents the groupoid scheme of formal group laws and strict isomorphisms, where $L$ is the Lazard ring and $L B \cong L [b_i | i \geq 0, b_0 =1]$ as a left $L$-algebra (cf. \cite{ravenel_green}).
nodes.statement_short: $(MU_*,MU_*MU)\cong(L,LB)$ represents formal group laws and strict isomorphisms, $LB\cong L[b_i]$.

nodes.name: Universal strict isomorphism b and logarithms log^L, log^R
nodes.statement: The $b_i's$ represent the universal strict isomorphism $\underline{b} (x) = \sum_i b_i x^{i+1}$ between the formal group laws defined respectively by the left and right units $\eta_L,\eta_R : L \rightrightarrows LB$, which are determined by their logarithms $\log^L$, $\log^R$ defined over $LB \otimes\mathbb{Q}$.

nodes.name: Exponential series exp^L, exp^R
nodes.statement: The exponential series $\exp^L, \exp^R$ over $LB \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ are the respective composition inverses of $\log^L, \log^R$.

nodes.name: b = exp^R composed with log^L
nodes.statement: The power series $\underline{b}$ satisfies the identity $ \underline{b} = \exp^R \circ \log ^L. $
conclusions: $ \underline{b} = \exp^R \circ \log ^L. $
nodes.label: lem:identify_b

nodes.name: Bernoulli numbers of a formal group law
nodes.statement: \cite[Definition 1.1]{miller} Let $F$ be a formal group law defined over a ring $R$. The Bernoulli numbers $B_n(F) \in R \otimes \mathbb{Q}$, for strictly positive integers $n \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$, are defined by \[ \frac{1}{\exp^F x} - \frac{1}{x} = \sum _{i\geq 0} \frac{B_{i+1}(F)}{(i+1)!} x^i, \] where $\exp^F(x) \in (R \otimes \mathbb{Q}) [[x]]$ is the exponential of $F$. The reduced Bernoulli number $\overline{B}_n (F)$ is defined as $\overline{B}_n (F) :=\frac{B_n (F)}{n} \in R \otimes \mathbb{Q}$.
nodes.statement_short: $B_n(F)$ are the coefficients of $1/\exp^F x - 1/x$; the reduced ones are $B_n(F)/n$.

nodes.name: Bernoulli numbers of KU
nodes.statement: For $n \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$, write $B_n^{KU} \in KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ (respectively $\overline{B}_n ^{KU} \in KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}$) for the Bernoulli number (resp. reduced Bernoulli number) associated to the orientation of $KU$. This is a graded form of the usual Bernoulli number $B_n$ (resp. reduced).

nodes.name: Degree of Bernoulli numbers
nodes.statement: If the formal group law $F$ is graded with respect to the usual conventions (so that the coordinate has degree $-2$), then $B_n (F)$ is a homogeneous element of degree $2n$.

nodes.name: Miller's divisibility theorem for reduced Bernoulli numbers
nodes.statement: Miller established the following fundamental divisibility property of the reduced Bernoulli numbers: if $R$ is a torsion free ring, then $d_n \overline{B}_n (F) \in R$, where $d_n$ is the order of the reduced Bernoulli number $\overline{B}_n $ in ${\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}}$ (see \cite[Theorem 1.3]{miller}).
assumptions: $R$ is a torsion free ring
conclusions: $d_n \overline{B}_n (F) \in R$

nodes.name: Thom spectrum CP^infty_n
nodes.statement: For $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, let $\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_n$ denote the Thom spectrum of the (virtual) bundle $n \lambda$ over $\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty$, where $\lambda$ denotes the canonical line bundle over $\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty$.

nodes.name: Module generators beta_i
nodes.statement: For $E$ a complex oriented ring spectrum, the Thom isomorphism implies that $E_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_n)$ is a free $E_*$-module on classes $\{\beta_i | i \geq n \}$. (The systems of generators as $n$ varies are compatible, hence $n$ will be omitted from the notation.)

nodes.name: Kunneth generators beta_i tensor beta_j
nodes.statement: There is a Künneth isomorphism $E_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_m \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty _n) \cong E_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_m) \otimes _{E_*} E_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_n)$, and the associated module generators will be written $\beta_i \otimes \beta_j$.

nodes.name: Generating series underline-beta
nodes.statement: For $E$ a complex oriented ring spectrum and $m,n$ integers, let $\underline{\beta}_m (S)$ denote the Laurent power series $\sum_{i \geq m} \beta_i S ^i$ over $E_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_m)$ and let $\underline{\beta}_m (S) \otimes \underline{\beta}_n (T)$ denote $\sum_{i \geq m, j \geq n} \beta_i \otimes \beta_j S ^iT^j$, defined over $E_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_m \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_n)$.

nodes.name: Comodule structure of MU_*(CP^infty_n)
nodes.statement: \cite[Proposition 3.3]{miller} Let $n$ be an integer, then the comodule structure $MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_n) \rightarrow MU_* MU \otimes_{MU_*} MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_n)$ is determined by \[ \underline{\beta}_n (S) \mapsto \underline{\beta}_n (\underline{b} (S) \otimes 1). \]
assumptions: $n$ be an integer
conclusions: the comodule structure $MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_n) \rightarrow MU_* MU \otimes_{MU_*} MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_n)$ is determined by \[ \underline{\beta}_n (S) \mapsto \underline{\beta}_n (\underline{b} (S) \otimes 1). \]
nodes.label: lem:comodule_cpn

nodes.name: Left versus right comodule conventions
nodes.statement: In the expression $\underline{\beta}_n (\underline{b} (x) \otimes 1)$, the elements $\beta_i$ are the module generators, which are usually written on the right when considering left $MU_*MU$-comodules. Miller \cite{miller} works with right comodules, where this notational issue does not arise.

nodes.name: Short exact sequence from the cofibre sequence of CP^infty_n
nodes.statement: The cofibre sequence of spectra (cf. \cite[section 2]{miller}): \begin{eqnarray} S^{2n} \rightarrow \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{n} \rightarrow \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{n+1} \rightarrow, \end{eqnarray} for $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, induces a short exact sequence of $MU_*MU$-comodules: \[ 0 \rightarrow MU_* [2n] \rightarrow MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_n) \rightarrow MU_*(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{n+1}) \rightarrow 0, \] where $[a]$ denotes the shift in degree, so that $(V_* [a])_t = V_{t-a}$, for a $\mathbb{Z}$-graded object $V_*$.
nodes.statement_short: The cofibre sequence $S^{2n}\to\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^\infty_n\to\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^\infty_{n+1}$ gives a short exact sequence of comodules; $[a]$ denotes degree shift.

nodes.name: Cofibre sequence of CP^infty_n (3)
nodes.statement: S^{2n} \rightarrow \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{n} \rightarrow \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{n+1} \rightarrow,
nodes.label: eqn:cofibre-CPn

nodes.name: Section sigma, retract r and section sigma'
nodes.statement: For $E$ a complex oriented ring spectrum, \begin{enumerate} \item let $\sigma : E_ * (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \rightarrow E_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1})$ be the section in $E_*$-modules defined by $\sigma (\beta_i) = \beta_i$ (for $i \geq 0$) and $r : E_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1}) \rightarrow E_*[-2]$ be the corresponding retract, which sends generators $\beta_i$, $i \geq 0$ to zero. \item let $\sigma' : E_ * (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \rightarrow E_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ denote the section $\sigma \otimes E_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: nota:sigma

nodes.name: S^1-transfer tau
nodes.statement: For $n=-1$, the connecting morphism of the cofibre sequence (\ref{eqn:cofibre-CPn}) defines the $S^1$-transfer $\tau : \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{0}\rightarrow S^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Double S^1-transfer
nodes.statement: The double $S^1$-transfer is the smash product $ \tau \wedge \tau : \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{0} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \rightarrow S^{-2}. $

nodes.name: Rational Thom class U and chromatic factorization tilde-tau of the single transfer
nodes.statement: The rational Thom class $U : \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1}\rightarrow S^{-2}_{\mathbb{Q}}$ induces a morphism of cofibre sequences \begin{eqnarray} \xymatrix{ S^{-2} \ar[r] \ar@{=}[d] & \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \ar[r] \ar[d]_U & \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \ar[r]^\tau \ar[d]^{\tilde{\tau}} & S^{-1} \ar@{=}[d] \\ S^{-2} \ar[r] &S^{-2}_{\mathbb{Q}} \ar[r] & S^{-2} _{\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}} \ar[r] & S ^{-1}, } \end{eqnarray} where $\tilde{\tau}$, the chromatic factorization of the single transfer, is determined uniquely by the commutativity of the right hand square.
nodes.statement_short: $U$ induces a map of cofibre sequences; $\tilde\tau:\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^\infty_0\to S^{-2}_{\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}}$ is the induced chromatic factorization of $\tau$.

nodes.name: Chromatic factorization of the single transfer (4)
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ S^{-2} \ar[r] \ar@{=}[d] & \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \ar[r] \ar[d]_U & \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \ar[r]^\tau \ar[d]^{\tilde{\tau}} & S^{-1} \ar@{=}[d] \\ S^{-2} \ar[r] &S^{-2}_{\mathbb{Q}} \ar[r] & S^{-2} _{\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}} \ar[r] & S ^{-1}, }
nodes.label: eqn:tau-tilde

nodes.name: MU_*(tilde-tau) determined by MU_*(U)
nodes.statement: The morphism of $MU_*MU$-comodules \[ MU_* (\tilde{\tau}) : MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \rightarrow MU_* \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}} [-2] \] is determined by the comodule morphism $MU_*(U) : MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1}) \rightarrow MU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-2]$, via the commutative diagram \begin{eqnarray} \xymatrix{ MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1}) \ar[r]^{MU_*(U)} & MU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-2] \ar@{->>}[d] \\ MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar@{.>}[u]^\sigma \ar[r]_(.45){MU_* (\tilde{\tau}) } & MU_* \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}} [-2], } \end{eqnarray} in which the solid arrows denote comodule morphisms.

nodes.name: Diagram relating MU_*(U), sigma and MU_*(tilde-tau) (5)
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1}) \ar[r]^{MU_*(U)} & MU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-2] \ar@{->>}[d] \\ MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar@{.>}[u]^\sigma \ar[r]_(.45){MU_* (\tilde{\tau}) } & MU_* \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}} [-2], }
nodes.label: eqn:U-sigma

nodes.name: MU_*(U) as a composite through rational homology
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lem:Landweber_exact}, the comodule morphism $MU_*(U)$ is the composite \[ \xymatrix{ MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1}) \ar[r] & MU_*MU \otimes _{MU_*} \mathbf{H}\mathbb{Q}_*(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1}) \ar[d]^{MU_*MU \otimes \mathbf{H}\mathbb{Q}_*(U)} \\ & MU_*MU \otimes _{MU*} \mathbb{Q} [-2] \ar[r]^(.6)\cong & MU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-2], } \] where $\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Q}$ is the rational Eilenberg-MacLane spectrum and the first morphism is the composite of the comodule structure morphism with $MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} ) \rightarrow \mathbf{H}\mathbb{Q}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1})$ induced by the canonical orientation of $\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Q}$.

nodes.name: MU-homology of the rational Thom class
nodes.statement: (Cf. \cite[Theorem 3.9]{miller}.) \begin{enumerate} \item The morphism $MU_* (U) :MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1}) \rightarrow MU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-2]$ is determined by \[ \underline{\beta}_{-1} (S) \mapsto \frac{1}{\log S}. \] \item The morphism of $MU_*$-modules $MU_* (U) \circ \sigma : MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 ) \rightarrow MU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-2]$ is determined by \[ \underline{\beta}_{0} (S) \mapsto \frac{1}{\log S} - \frac{1}{S}. \] \item The morphism $MU_* (\tilde{\tau}) $ is the composite of $MU_*(U) \circ \sigma$ with the projection $MU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-2]\twoheadrightarrow MU_* \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}}[-2]$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $MU_*(U)$ sends $\underline\beta_{-1}(S)$ to $1/\log S$; composing with $\sigma$ gives $1/\log S-1/S$, which reduces to $MU_*(\tilde\tau)$.
conclusions: The morphism $MU_* (U) :MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1}) \rightarrow MU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-2]$ is determined by \[ \underline{\beta}_{-1} (S) \mapsto \frac{1}{\log S}. \]

The morphism of $MU_*$-modules $MU_* (U) \circ \sigma : MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 ) \rightarrow MU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-2]$ is determined by \[ \underline{\beta}_{0} (S) \mapsto \frac{1}{\log S} - \frac{1}{S}. \]
The morphism $MU_* (\tilde{\tau}) $ is the composite of $MU_*(U) \circ \sigma$ with the projection $MU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-2]\twoheadrightarrow MU_* \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}}[-2]$
nodes.label: lem:MUThom

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.11
nodes.statement: The first statement follows from the comodule structure of $MU_*(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1})$ together with the fact that, under the morphism $MU_* MU \otimes \mathbb{Q} \cong MU_* \otimes MU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} \rightarrow MU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ induced by the augmentation $MU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} \rightarrow \mathbb{Q}$ on the right hand factor, $\exp^R (S) \mapsto S$, so that $\underline{b} (S) \mapsto \log (S)$. The section $\sigma$ is determined by $\underline{\beta}_0 (S) \mapsto \underline{\beta}_{-1} (S) - \beta_{-1}\frac{1}{S}$, which gives the second statement, by composition. The final statement follows from the commutativity of diagram (\ref{eqn:U-sigma}).
nodes.statement_short: Apply the augmentation to the comodule structure ($\underline b(S)\mapsto\log S$), then compose with $\sigma$ and use diagram (5).

nodes.name: First statement
nodes.statement: The first statement follows from the comodule structure of $MU_*(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1})$ together with the fact that, under the morphism $MU_* MU \otimes \mathbb{Q} \cong MU_* \otimes MU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} \rightarrow MU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ induced by the augmentation $MU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} \rightarrow \mathbb{Q}$ on the right hand factor, $\exp^R (S) \mapsto S$, so that $\underline{b} (S) \mapsto \log (S)$.
nodes.statement_short: Augment the comodule structure: $\underline b(S)\mapsto\log S$.

nodes.name: Second statement
nodes.statement: The section $\sigma$ is determined by $\underline{\beta}_0 (S) \mapsto \underline{\beta}_{-1} (S) - \beta_{-1}\frac{1}{S}$, which gives the second statement, by composition.
nodes.statement_short: Compose with the section $\sigma$.

nodes.name: Third statement
nodes.statement: The final statement follows from the commutativity of diagram (\ref{eqn:U-sigma}).
nodes.statement_short: Conclude from diagram (5).

nodes.name: Chromatic factorization of the double transfer (Hilditch)
nodes.statement: \cite{BCGHRW} Let $p \geq 3$ be a prime. There exists a morphism $\Theta : \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \rightarrow L_1 S^{-4}/p^\infty$ which fits into a commutative square: \begin{eqnarray} \xymatrix{ \Sigma^{-2} \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \ar[r] \ar[d]_{\Sigma^{-2}\tilde{\tau}} & \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \ar[d]^\Theta \\ S^{-4} /p^\infty \ar[r] & L_1 S ^{-4}/p^\infty, } \end{eqnarray} where the top morphism is induced by the inclusion of the bottom cell $S^{-2} \rightarrow \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1}$. Moreover, for any extension to a morphism of cofibre sequences: \[ \xymatrix{ \Sigma^{-2} \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \ar[r] \ar[d]_{\Sigma^{-2}\tilde{\tau}} & \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \ar[d]^\Theta \ar[r] & \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \ar[d]^{\overline{\Theta}} \ar[r]^(.6){\tau \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0} & \Sigma ^{-1}\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \ar[d]^{\Sigma^{-1} \tilde{\tau}} \\ S^{-4} /p^\infty \ar[r] & L_1 S ^{-4}/p^\infty \ar[r] & S^{-4} /p^\infty , v_1^\infty \ar[r] & S^{-3}/p^\infty, } \] where the top row is the cofibre sequence $(S^{-2}\rightarrow \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \rightarrow \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 $ and the bottom row is the cofibre sequence associated to $L_1$-localization, $\overline{\Theta} : \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \rightarrow S^{-4} /p^\infty , v_1^\infty$ provides a factorization of the double transfer morphism across the chromatic morphism $S^{-4} /p^\infty , v_1^\infty \rightarrow S^{-2}$.
nodes.section: 3.3 The chromatic factorization of the double transfer
nodes.origin_citation: Baker, Carlisle, Gray, Hilditch, Ray, Wood 1988 (attributed to Hilditch)
nodes.statement_short: For $p\ge3$ there is $\Theta$ extending $\Sigma^{-2}\tilde\tau$, and any extension $\overline\Theta$ factors the double transfer through $S^{-4}/p^\infty,v_1^\infty$.

nodes.name: Eigenspace construction of theta
nodes.statement: The construction of $\theta$ is by an eigenspace argument for the action of the Adams operation $\psi^\gamma$, where $\gamma \in \mathbb{Z}$ is a topological generator of $\mathbb{Z}_p$ (compare Proposition \ref{prop:represent-ad}); this is made explicit in the proof of \cite[Proposition 2.4]{imaoka}, which generalizes this result.

nodes.name: Power series tilde-theta'
nodes.statement: Let $\tilde{\theta} ' (S,T) $ denote the power series in $KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} [[S,T]]$ \[ \sum _{i, j >0}\frac{B_i^{KU}}{i!}\frac{B_j^{KU}}{j!} \left( \frac{\gamma^i -1}{\gamma^{i+j}-1} \right) (\log^{KU} S)^{i-1}(\log ^{KU} T) ^{j-1}, \] where $\log^{KU}$ is the logarithm of the multiplicative formal group law of $KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}$.

nodes.name: Choice of theta
nodes.statement: Let $\theta : \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \rightarrow \Sigma ^{-4} KU_{\mathbb{Q}}$ be the class which is determined by $\tilde{\theta}_* : KU_*(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1}\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \rightarrow KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4]$: \[ \underline{\beta}_{-1}(S) \otimes \underline{ \beta}_0(T) \mapsto \frac{1}{S} \left(\frac{1}{\log^{KU}T} - \frac{1}{T}\right) + \tilde{\theta}' (S,T). \]

nodes.statement_short: $\theta$ is the class whose $KU$-homology map is $\frac1S(\frac1{\log^{KU}T}-\frac1T)+\tilde\theta'(S,T)$.

nodes.name: MU-homology of the chromatic factorization of the double transfer
nodes.statement: Let $p$ be an odd prime. There is a commutative diagram of morphisms of $MU_*MU$-comodules: \[ \xymatrix{ & MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1}\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar@{->>}[r] \ar@/_1pc/[ld]_(.6){MU_*(\theta)} \ar[d]^{MU_*(\Theta)} & MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{0}\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar[d]^{MU_*(\overline{\Theta})} \\ MU_* KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}[-4] \ar@{->>}@/_1pc/[rd] & MU_*/p^\infty[v_1^{-1}] [-4] \ar@{^(->}[d] \ar@{->>}[r]^{\mathrm{pr}} & MU_* /p^\infty,v_1^\infty [-4] \ar@{^(->}[d] \\ & MU_* KU /p^\infty[-4] \ar@{->>}[r] & (MU_* KU /p^\infty)/(MU_*/p^\infty)[-4]. } \] \begin{enumerate} \item The underlying $MU_*$-module morphism of $MU_* (\overline{\Theta})$ is the composite $\mathrm{pr}\circ MU_* (\Theta) \circ \sigma'$. \item The morphism $MU_*({\Theta})$ is determined by the comodule morphism $MU_* (\theta)$ and hence by the morphism $\tilde{\theta}_* : KU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1}\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 )\rightarrow KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}$. \item The morphism $MU_*(\overline{\Theta})$ is determined by the comodule morphism $MU_* (\theta)$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $MU_*(\Theta)$ and $MU_*(\overline\Theta)$ fit in a comodule diagram and are determined by $MU_*(\theta)$, hence by $\tilde\theta_*$.
assumptions: $p$ be an odd prime
conclusions: There is a commutative diagram of morphisms of $MU_*MU$-comodules: \[ \xymatrix{ & MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1}\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar@{->>}[r] \ar@/_1pc/[ld]_(.6){MU_*(\theta)} \ar[d]^{MU_*(\Theta)} & MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{0}\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar[d]^{MU_*(\overline{\Theta})} \\ MU_* KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}[-4] \ar@{->>}@/_1pc/[rd] & MU_*/p^\infty[v_1^{-1}] [-4] \ar@{^(->}[d] \ar@{->>}[r]^{\mathrm{pr}} & MU_* /p^\infty,v_1^\infty [-4] \ar@{^(->}[d] \\ & MU_* KU /p^\infty[-4] \ar@{->>}[r] & (MU_* KU /p^\infty)/(MU_*/p^\infty)[-4]. } \]
The underlying $MU_*$-module morphism of $MU_* (\overline{\Theta})$ is the composite $\mathrm{pr}\circ MU_* (\Theta) \circ \sigma'$

The morphism $MU_*({\Theta})$ is determined by the comodule morphism $MU_* (\theta)$ and hence by the morphism $\tilde{\theta}_* : KU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1}\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 )\rightarrow KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}$
The morphism $MU_*(\overline{\Theta})$ is determined by the comodule morphism $MU_* (\theta)$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.16
nodes.statement: The commutativity of the left hand part of the diagram follows from Proposition \ref{prop:f,g-Landweber} and the upper right hand square is induced by the morphism of cofibre sequences defining $\overline{\Theta}$. The lower right hand square is induced by the monomorphism given by the Hattori-Stong theorem (see Lemma \ref{lem:hattori-stong}) \[ MU_* /p^\infty [v_1^{-1}] \hookrightarrow MU_ * KU /p^\infty, \] since the kernel to the projection $MU_* /p^\infty [v_1^{-1}] \twoheadrightarrow MU_*/p^\infty , v_1^\infty $ is $MU_* /p^\infty$. The morphism $MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \twoheadrightarrow MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ admits the section $\sigma'$ in $MU_*$-modules, hence the identification of the underlying module morphism of $MU_* (\overline{\Theta})$ follows from the upper right hand square. For part \ref{thm_item:Theta}, the injectivity of $MU_* /p^\infty, v_1 ^\infty [-4] \hookrightarrow MU_* KU /p^\infty[-4]$ and the commutativity of the left hand square implies that $ MU_* (\theta)$ determines $MU_* ({\Theta})$ as a morphism of $MU_*MU$-comodules. The morphism $MU_* (\theta)$ is determined by $\tilde{\theta}_* : KU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1}\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 )\rightarrow KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}$, by the second part of Proposition \ref{prop:f,g-Landweber}. The final statement follows from the commutativity of the lower right hand square.
nodes.statement_short: Combine Proposition 2.7 for the left square with the Hattori-Stong monomorphism and the section $\sigma'$.

nodes.name: Commutativity of the diagram
nodes.statement: The commutativity of the left hand part of the diagram follows from Proposition \ref{prop:f,g-Landweber} and the upper right hand square is induced by the morphism of cofibre sequences defining $\overline{\Theta}$. The lower right hand square is induced by the monomorphism given by the Hattori-Stong theorem (see Lemma \ref{lem:hattori-stong}) \[ MU_* /p^\infty [v_1^{-1}] \hookrightarrow MU_ * KU /p^\infty, \] since the kernel to the projection $MU_* /p^\infty [v_1^{-1}] \twoheadrightarrow MU_*/p^\infty , v_1^\infty $ is $MU_* /p^\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Left part from Proposition 2.7, right squares from the cofibre sequences and Hattori-Stong.

nodes.name: Part (1)
nodes.statement: The morphism $MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \twoheadrightarrow MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ admits the section $\sigma'$ in $MU_*$-modules, hence the identification of the underlying module morphism of $MU_* (\overline{\Theta})$ follows from the upper right hand square.
nodes.statement_short: Use the section $\sigma'$ to identify the module map of $MU_*(\overline\Theta)$.

nodes.name: Part (2)
nodes.statement: For part \ref{thm_item:Theta}, the injectivity of $MU_* /p^\infty, v_1 ^\infty [-4] \hookrightarrow MU_* KU /p^\infty[-4]$ and the commutativity of the left hand square implies that $ MU_* (\theta)$ determines $MU_* ({\Theta})$ as a morphism of $MU_*MU$-comodules. The morphism $MU_* (\theta)$ is determined by $\tilde{\theta}_* : KU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1}\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 )\rightarrow KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}$, by the second part of Proposition \ref{prop:f,g-Landweber}.
nodes.statement_short: Injectivity plus Proposition 2.7(2).

nodes.name: Part (3)
nodes.statement: The final statement follows from the commutativity of the lower right hand square.
nodes.statement_short: Read off from the lower right square.

nodes.name: Logarithms log^MU, log^KU and the series b'
nodes.statement: The torsion-free ring $MU_*KU$ has two formal group law structures, corresponding to the left and right units $MU_* \rightarrow MU_*KU$ and $KU_* \rightarrow MU_* KU$ respectively; write $\log^{MU}$ and $\log^{KU}$ for the respective logarithms defined over $MU_* KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ and set $\underline{b}' = \exp^{KU} \circ \log^{MU}$, which identifies with the image of $\underline{b}$ under $MU_*MU \rightarrow MU_*KU$.

nodes.name: Formula for MU_*(theta)
nodes.statement: \ \begin{enumerate} \item The morphism $MU_*(\theta)\in \mathrm{Hom}_{MU_*MU} (MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 ), MU_* KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}[-4]) $ is determined by $ \underline{\beta}_{-1} (S) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (T) \mapsto $ \[ \frac{1}{\underline{b}'(S)} \Big(\frac{1}{\log^{MU} T} - \frac{1}{\underline{b}' (T) }\Big) + \sum _{i, j >0}\frac{B_i^{KU}}{i!}\frac{B_j^{KU}}{j!} \left( \frac{\gamma^i -1}{\gamma^{i+j}-1} \right) (\log^{MU} S)^{i-1}(\log ^{MU} T) ^{j-1}. \] \item The morphism $MU_*(\theta) \circ \sigma' \in \mathrm{Hom}_{MU_*} (MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 ), MU_* KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}[-4]) $ is determined by $ \underline{\beta}_0 (S) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (T) \mapsto $ \[ \Big( \frac{1}{\underline{b}'(S)}- \frac{1}{S}\Big) \Big(\frac{1}{\log^{MU} T} - \frac{1}{\underline{b}' (T) }\Big) + \sum _{i, j >0}\frac{B_i^{KU}}{i!}\frac{B_j^{KU}}{j!} \left( \frac{\gamma^i -1}{\gamma^{i+j}-1} \right) (\log^{MU} S)^{i-1}(\log ^{MU} T) ^{j-1}. \] \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Explicit generating-series formulas for $MU_*(\theta)$ and $MU_*(\theta)\circ\sigma'$ in terms of $\underline b'$, $\log^{MU}$ and $KU$ Bernoulli numbers.
conclusions: The morphism $MU_*(\theta)\in \mathrm{Hom}_{MU_*MU} (MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 ), MU_* KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}[-4]) $ is determined by $ \underline{\beta}_{-1} (S) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (T) \mapsto $ \[ \frac{1}{\underline{b}'(S)} \Big(\frac{1}{\log^{MU} T} - \frac{1}{\underline{b}' (T) }\Big) + \sum _{i, j >0}\frac{B_i^{KU}}{i!}\frac{B_j^{KU}}{j!} \left( \frac{\gamma^i -1}{\gamma^{i+j}-1} \right) (\log^{MU} S)^{i-1}(\log ^{MU} T) ^{j-1}. \]

The morphism $MU_*(\theta) \circ \sigma' \in \mathrm{Hom}_{MU_*} (MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 ), MU_* KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}[-4]) $ is determined by $ \underline{\beta}_0 (S) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (T) \mapsto $ \[ \Big( \frac{1}{\underline{b}'(S)}- \frac{1}{S}\Big) \Big(\frac{1}{\log^{MU} T} - \frac{1}{\underline{b}' (T) }\Big) + \sum _{i, j >0}\frac{B_i^{KU}}{i!}\frac{B_j^{KU}}{j!} \left( \frac{\gamma^i -1}{\gamma^{i+j}-1} \right) (\log^{MU} S)^{i-1}(\log ^{MU} T) ^{j-1}. \]
nodes.label: prop:MUtheta_sigmap

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.17
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{prop:f,g-Landweber}, the morphism $MU_* (\theta)$ is determined by the commutative diagram \[ \xymatrix{ MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar[rr]^(.4){\psi _{MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)}} \ar[d]_{MU_* (\theta)} &\ & MU_*MU \otimes_{MU_*} MU_*(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar[d] \\ MU_*MU\otimes_{MU_*} KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4] && MU_*MU \otimes _{MU_*} KU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar[ll]^{MU_*MU \otimes \tilde{\theta}_*}. } \] Lemma \ref{lem:comodule_cpn} implies that the comodule structure of $MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ is determined by \[ \underline{\beta}_{-1} (S) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (T) \mapsto \underline{\beta}_{-1} (\underline{b}(S)\otimes 1) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (\underline{b}(T) \otimes 1). \] Composing with the morphism induced by $\theta$ and using the identity $\underline{b}' = \exp^{KU} \circ \log^{MU}$ shows that $MU_* (\theta)$ is given by $\underline{\beta}_{-1} (S) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (T) \mapsto$ \[ \frac{1}{\underline{b}'(S)} \Big(\frac{1}{\log^{MU} T} - \frac{1}{\underline{b}' (T) }\Big) + \sum _{i, j >0}\frac{B_i^{KU}}{i!}\frac{B_j^{KU}}{j!} \left( \frac{\gamma^i -1}{\gamma^{i+j}-1} \right) (\log^{MU} S)^{i-1}(\log ^{MU} T) ^{j-1}. \] The second statement is proved by composing with the morphism $\sigma'$, which is represented by \[ \underline{\beta}_0 (S) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (T) \mapsto \underline{\beta}_{-1} (S) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (T) - \beta_{-1} \frac{1}{S} \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (T). \] The morphism $MU_* (\theta)$ restricts to give: \[ \beta_{-1} \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (T) \mapsto \frac{1} {log^{MU} T} - \frac{1}{\underline{b}'(T)}. \] The result follows.
nodes.statement_short: Compute via Proposition 2.7: apply the comodule structure of Lemma 3.8, then $\tilde\theta_*$, using $\underline b'=\exp^{KU}\circ\log^{MU}$; then compose with $\sigma'$.

nodes.name: Reduce to a diagram
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{prop:f,g-Landweber}, the morphism $MU_* (\theta)$ is determined by the commutative diagram \[ \xymatrix{ MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar[rr]^(.4){\psi _{MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)}} \ar[d]_{MU_* (\theta)} &\ & MU_*MU \otimes_{MU_*} MU_*(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar[d] \\ MU_*MU\otimes_{MU_*} KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4] && MU_*MU \otimes _{MU_*} KU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar[ll]^{MU_*MU \otimes \tilde{\theta}_*}. } \]
nodes.statement_short: By Proposition 2.7, $MU_*(\theta)$ is $\tilde\theta_*$ after the comodule structure map.

nodes.name: Comodule structure
nodes.statement: Lemma \ref{lem:comodule_cpn} implies that the comodule structure of $MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ is determined by \[ \underline{\beta}_{-1} (S) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (T) \mapsto \underline{\beta}_{-1} (\underline{b}(S)\otimes 1) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (\underline{b}(T) \otimes 1). \]
nodes.statement_short: Comodule structure of the smash product via Lemma 3.8.

nodes.name: First formula
nodes.statement: Composing with the morphism induced by $\theta$ and using the identity $\underline{b}' = \exp^{KU} \circ \log^{MU}$ shows that $MU_* (\theta)$ is given by $\underline{\beta}_{-1} (S) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (T) \mapsto$ \[ \frac{1}{\underline{b}'(S)} \Big(\frac{1}{\log^{MU} T} - \frac{1}{\underline{b}' (T) }\Big) + \sum _{i, j >0}\frac{B_i^{KU}}{i!}\frac{B_j^{KU}}{j!} \left( \frac{\gamma^i -1}{\gamma^{i+j}-1} \right) (\log^{MU} S)^{i-1}(\log ^{MU} T) ^{j-1}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Compose with $\tilde\theta_*$, giving part (1).

nodes.name: Section sigma'
nodes.statement: The second statement is proved by composing with the morphism $\sigma'$, which is represented by \[ \underline{\beta}_0 (S) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (T) \mapsto \underline{\beta}_{-1} (S) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (T) - \beta_{-1} \frac{1}{S} \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (T). \]
nodes.statement_short: Write down $\sigma'$ on generating series.

nodes.name: Second formula
nodes.statement: The morphism $MU_* (\theta)$ restricts to give: \[ \beta_{-1} \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (T) \mapsto \frac{1} {log^{MU} T} - \frac{1}{\underline{b}'(T)}. \] The result follows.
nodes.statement_short: Restrict $MU_*(\theta)$ to $\beta_{-1}$ terms and conclude.

nodes.name: Algebraic transfer class [e_tau]
nodes.statement: The cofibre sequence defining the transfer $\tau : \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \rightarrow S^{-1}$ induces a short exact sequence of $MU_*MU$-comodules and hence an algebraic transfer class: \[ [e_\tau] \in \mathrm{Ext}^1_{MU_* MU}(MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0),MU_* [-2]). \]

nodes.name: Algebraic double transfer
nodes.statement: The algebraic double transfer is the class: \[ [e_\tau]^2\in \mathrm{Ext}^2_{MU_* MU}(MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 ),MU_* [-4]) \] given by Yoneda product.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.2 (standard cocycle choice)
nodes.statement: Proposition \ref{prop:cocycle-canonical-splitting} applied with respect to the section $\sigma$ gives the standard choice $e_\tau$ of representing cocycle:
nodes.statement_short: Apply Proposition A.8 with the section $\sigma$.

nodes.name: Cocycle e_tau
nodes.statement: The cocycle $ {e_\tau} \in \mathrm{Hom}_{MU_*}(MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0), MU_* MU[-2]) $ is determined by \[ \underline{\beta}_{0} (S) \mapsto \frac{1}{S} - \frac{1}{\underline{b} (S)} . \]
conclusions: The cocycle $ {e_\tau} \in \mathrm{Hom}_{MU_*}(MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0), MU_* MU[-2]) $ is determined by \[ \underline{\beta}_{0} (S) \mapsto \frac{1}{S} - \frac{1}{\underline{b} (S)} . \]

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.3 (sketch)
nodes.statement: Diagram (\ref{eqn:tau-tilde}) induces a morphism of short exact sequences of $MU_*MU$-comodules: \[ \xymatrix{ 0 \ar[r] & MU_* [-2] \ar@{=}[d] \ar[r] & MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} ) \ar[d]^{MU_* (U)} \ar[r] & MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar[d]^{MU_*(\tilde{\tau})} \ar[r] & 0 \\ 0 \ar[r] & MU_* [-2] \ar[r] & MU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-2] \ar[r] & MU_* \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}} [-2] \ar[r] & 0. } \] The morphism $\tilde{\tau}$ provides a chromatic factorization of the single transfer $\tau$; this corresponds to the following result, which can be proved using Proposition \ref{prop:cocycle-canonical-splitting}.
nodes.statement_short: Diagram (4) gives a morphism of short exact sequences; the identity follows from Proposition A.8.

conclusions: [e_\tau] = \partial_1 MU_* (\tilde{\tau}),

nodes.name: Class [E_tau]
nodes.statement: Forming the tensor product $[e_\tau] \otimes MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ gives a class \[ [E_\tau ]\in \mathrm{Ext}^1_{MU_* MU}(MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0),MU_*(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) [-2]). \]

nodes.name: Cocycle E_tau
nodes.statement: The class $[E_\tau]$ is represented by the cocycle \[ {E_\tau} \in \mathrm{Hom}_{MU_*}(MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0), MU_* MU\otimes _{MU_*} MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)[-2]) \] defined with respect to the section $\sigma'$, which is given by \[ \underline{\beta}_ 0 (S) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (T) \mapsto \Big( \frac{1}{S} - \frac{1}{\underline{b}(S)} \Big) \underline{\beta}_0 (\underline{b}(T)). \]
conclusions: The class $[E_\tau]$ is represented by the cocycle \[ {E_\tau} \in \mathrm{Hom}_{MU_*}(MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0), MU_* MU\otimes _{MU_*} MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)[-2]) \] defined with respect to the section $\sigma'$, which is given by \[ \underline{\beta}_ 0 (S) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (T) \mapsto \Big( \frac{1}{S} - \frac{1}{\underline{b}(S)} \Big) \underline{\beta}_0 (\underline{b}(T)). \]
nodes.label: lem:Etau

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.4
nodes.statement: Apply Proposition \ref{prop:cocycle-canonical-splitting} with respect to the section $\sigma'$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Proposition A.8 with the section $\sigma'$.

nodes.name: Class [kappa]

nodes.name: Double transfer is the chromatic boundary of [kappa]

conclusions: [e_\tau]^2 = \partial_1 [\kappa],

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.6
nodes.statement: Straightforward.
nodes.statement_short: Asserted to be straightforward.

nodes.name: Cocycle kappa
nodes.statement: The class $[\kappa]$ is represented by the standard choice $\kappa$ of cocycle, constructed with respect to the section $\sigma'$: \[ {\kappa} \in \mathrm{Hom}_{MU_*} ( MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0),MU_*MU \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}} [-4]). \]

nodes.name: Morphism K
nodes.statement: Write $K \in \mathrm{Hom}_{MU_*} (MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0), MU_*MU \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4])$ for the composite morphism of $MU_*$-modules: \[ \xymatrix{ MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar[r]^(.4){E_\tau} \ar[rd]_K & MU_* MU\otimes _{MU_*}MU_*(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{0})[-2] \ar[d]^{MU_*MU \otimes MU_*(U) \circ \sigma } \\ & MU_*MU \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4]. } \]

nodes.name: Formula for K and kappa
nodes.statement: \ \begin{enumerate} \item The class $[\kappa]$ is represented by the cocyle $\kappa$ given by reduction of the morphism $K$ via $MU_*MU \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4] \rightarrow MU_*MU \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}}[-4]$. \item The morphism $K \in \mathrm{Hom}_{MU_*} (MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0), MU_*MU \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4])$ is determined by \[ \underline{\beta}_0 (S) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (T) \mapsto \Big( \frac{1}{S}- \frac{1}{\underline{b}(S)} \Big) \Big( \frac{1}{\log^L T } - \frac{1}{\underline{b}(T)} \Big). \] \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $\kappa$ is the reduction of $K$, and $K$ sends $\underline\beta_0(S)\otimes\underline\beta_0(T)$ to $(1/S-1/\underline b(S))(1/\log^L T-1/\underline b(T))$.
conclusions: The class $[\kappa]$ is represented by the cocyle $\kappa$ given by reduction of the morphism $K$ via $MU_*MU \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4] \rightarrow MU_*MU \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}}[-4]$

The morphism $K \in \mathrm{Hom}_{MU_*} (MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0), MU_*MU \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4])$ is determined by \[ \underline{\beta}_0 (S) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (T) \mapsto \Big( \frac{1}{S}- \frac{1}{\underline{b}(S)} \Big) \Big( \frac{1}{\log^L T } - \frac{1}{\underline{b}(T)} \Big). \]

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.8
nodes.statement: The first statement follows from the construction of $K$. The second follows from Lemma \ref{lem:Etau}, by composition with the morphism $MU_*MU \otimes (MU_*(U) \circ\sigma)$ (see Lemma \ref{lem:MUThom}), using the identity $\log^L = \log^R \circ \underline{b}$ of Lemma \ref{lem:identify_b}.

$\partial_2 MU_* (\overline{\Theta}) $ is independent of the choice of $\overline{\Theta}$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.9
nodes.statement: The morphism $MU_* (\Theta)$ gives rise to a morphism between short exact sequences of $MU_*MU$-comodules: \[ \xymatrix{ 0 \ar[r] & MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)[-2] \ar[d]_{MU_* (\tilde{\tau}) [-2]} \ar[r] & MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar[r] \ar[d]_{MU_* (\Theta)} & MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar[d]^{MU_* (\overline{\Theta}) } \ar[r] & 0 \\ 0 \ar[r] & MU_*/p^\infty[-4] \ar[r] & MU_* /p^\infty [v_1]^{-1}[-4] \ar[r] & MU_* /p^\infty , v_1 ^\infty [-4] \ar[r] & 0, } \] where the top row represents $[E_\tau]$. By definition, $[\kappa] = MU_* (\tilde{\tau}) [E_\tau]$ and $\partial _2 MU_* (\overline{\Theta})$ is represented by the pullback of the lower short exact sequence along $MU_* (\overline{\Theta})$. Forming the pushout of the top sequence using $MU_* (\tilde{\tau}) $ and the pullback of the lower sequence via $MU_* (\overline{\Theta})$ gives Yoneda-equivalent short exact sequences, which therefore define the same class in $\mathrm{Ext}^1$, as required.

nodes.name: Base-changed morphism _{MU_*}K_{KU_*}
nodes.statement: The morphism $MU_*MU \rightarrow MU_* KU$ associated to the orientation of $KU$ induces the morphism (using the notation introduced in Section \ref{sect:cocycle-basechange}): \[ _{MU_*} K _{KU_*} \in \mathrm{Hom}_{MU_*} (MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0), MU_*KU \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4]). \]

nodes.statement: This can be identified with the composite \[ \xymatrix{ MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar[r]^{- \sigma'} & MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar[r]^(.35){\psi} & MU_*MU \otimes_{MU_*} MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar[d] \\ & MU_* KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}[-4] & MU_*MU \otimes_{MU_*} KU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar[l], } \] where $\psi$ is the comodule structure map, the vertical arrow is induced by the orientation of $KU$ and the final morphism of $MU_*MU$-modules is defined by the composite \begin{eqnarray} KU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \twoheadrightarrow KU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) [-2] \stackrel{KU_*(U) \circ \sigma}{\longrightarrow} KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4] \end{eqnarray} of the projection induced by $KU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1}) \twoheadrightarrow KU_* [-2]$ with the morphism induced by the rational Thom class of $\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.12
nodes.statement: The second morphism in (\ref{eqn:KU_thom_sigma}) is related to the morphism $\tilde{\theta}_* : KU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \rightarrow KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4]$ via the following commutative diagram derived from Theorem \ref{thm:MU-thetas}: \[ \xymatrix{ \Sigma^{-2} \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \ar[r] \ar[d]_{\Sigma^{-2}U} & \Sigma^{-2} \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \ar[d]_{\Sigma^{-2}\tilde{\tau}} \ar[r] & \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \ar[d]^{\Theta} \ar[ldd]|\hole_(.3)\theta \\ S^{-4}_{\mathbb{Q}} \ar[r] \ar[rd] & S^{-4}/p^\infty \ar[r] & L_1 S^{-4} /p^\infty \ar[d] \\ & \Sigma^{-4} KU_{\mathbb{Q}} \ar[r] & \Sigma^{-4} KU/p^\infty. } \] This implies the following result (which corresponds to a fundamental property of $\theta$ used in the construction of $\Theta$).

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.14

nodes.statement: For $X$ a spectrum, there is a natural commutative diagram of graded abelian groups, induced by the orientation of ${\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}}$ and rationalization \[ \xymatrix{ \mathbf{P} MU_* X \ar@{^(->}[r] \ar[d] & MU_* X \ar[r] & \mathbb{Z} \otimes_{MU_* } MU_* (X) \ar[r] & {\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}}_* X \ar[d] \\ \mathbf{P} MU_* X \otimes \mathbb{Q} \ar[rrr]_\cong &&& \mathbf{H}\mathbb{Q}_* X, } \] in which the lower horizontal morphism is an isomorphism. nodes.name: Primitives of smash powers of CP^infty as divided power subalgebra
nodes.statement: Let $d$ be a natural number. Then $$ \mathbf{P} MU_* ((\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)^{\wedge d}) \hookrightarrow {\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}}_* ((\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)^{\wedge d}) $$ is a morphism of algebras, where the product is induced by the $H$-space structure of $\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty$. The homology ${\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}}_* ((\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)^{\wedge d})$ is the free divided power algebra $\Gamma^* (\mathbb{Z}^{\oplus d}) $, hence $ \mathbf{P} MU_* ((\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)^{\wedge d})$ is a subalgebra of $\Gamma^* (\mathbb{Z}^{\oplus d}) $.

nodes.name: Primitive generators p_n
nodes.statement: The primitives $ \mathbf{P} MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ were calculated by David Segal \cite{segal}; an elegant approach is given by Miller in \cite[Proposition 4.1]{miller}, where the primitive generators $p_n \in MU_{2n}(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ are defined by means of the expansion \[ \underline{\beta}_0(\exp (T)) = \sum \frac{p_n}{n!}T^n \] in $MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \otimes \mathbb{Q}$, so that $|p_n|= 2n$.

nodes.name: Hurewicz image of the primitive generators
nodes.statement: The morphism $ \mathbf{P} MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \rightarrow {\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) $ sends $p_n$ to $ (\beta_1^{\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}})^n = n! \beta_n^{\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}}$, where the $\beta_i^{\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}}$ denote the canonical module generators of ${\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ (cf. \cite[Remark 4.2]{miller}).
conclusions: sends $p_n$ to $ (\beta_1^{\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}})^n = n! \beta_n^{\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}}$

nodes.name: p_i tensor p_j are primitives
nodes.statement: By the Künneth isomorphism $MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \cong MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \otimes_{MU_*} MU_*(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$, for pairs of natural numbers $(i,j)$, $p_i \otimes p_j$ is a primitive of $MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$.

nodes.name: Integral primitives of MU_*(CP^infty x CP^infty)
nodes.statement: The integral calculation of $\mathbf{P} MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ is an interesting and difficult problem: the elements $p_i \otimes p_j$ do not generate the primitives, due to delicate divisibility questions (cf. \cite{knapp_habilit}, \cite{baker_transfer} and \cite{BCRS}, for example).
nodes.origin_citation: Knapp 1979; Baker 1988; Baker, Clarke, Ray, Schwartz 1989
nodes.statement_short: Determine $\mathbf{P}MU_*(\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ integrally; the $p_i\otimes p_j$ do not generate it.

nodes.name: Rational basis of the primitives of MU_*(CP_0 smash CP_0)
nodes.statement: The primitive $\mathbf{P} MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ subgroup is a graded free $\mathbb{Z}$-module such that $\mathbf{P} MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ has basis $\{ p_i \otimes p_j | i, j \geq 0 \}$.
conclusions: The primitive $\mathbf{P} MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ subgroup is a graded free $\mathbb{Z}$-module such that $\mathbf{P} MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ has basis $\{ p_i \otimes p_j | i, j \geq 0 \}$.

nodes.name: Generating series of primitives frak-p(S,T)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathfrak{p} (S, T) $ denote the two-variable power-series in $MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 ) \otimes \mathbb{Q} [[S, T]]$: \[ \mathfrak{p}(S, T):= \sum_{m,n \geq 0} p_m \otimes p_n \frac{S^m T^n}{m! n !}. \]

nodes.name: Generating series identity for primitives
nodes.statement: There is an identity of formal power series: \[ \mathfrak{p}(S, T) = \underline{\beta}_0 (\exp S) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (\exp T). \]
conclusions: \mathfrak{p}(S, T) = \underline{\beta}_0 (\exp S) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (\exp T).

nodes.name: Primitive as a comodule morphism
nodes.statement: A primitive $\mathfrak{p}$ of degree $2k$ in $MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ corresponds to a morphism of comodules \[ \mathfrak{p} \in \mathrm{Hom}_{MU_* MU}(MU_* [2k] , MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)). \]

nodes.statement: This induces a class $\mathfrak{p}^* [\kappa] \in \mathrm{Ext}^1_{MU_*MU} (MU_* [2k] , MU_* \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}} [-4])$ and, by the chromatic connecting morphism $\partial_1$, the image of the double algebraic transfer: \[ \mathfrak{p} ^* [e_\tau^2] = \partial_1 \mathfrak{p}^* [\kappa] \in \mathrm{Ext}^2 _{MU_*MU} (MU_*[2k] , MU_* [-4]), \] where the identification follows from Proposition \ref{prop:kappa-transfer}.

nodes.name: Left and right reduced Bernoulli numbers in MU_*MU

assumptions: for natural numbers $m,n$
conclusions: K (p_m \otimes p_n) = (\overline{B}^R_{m+1} - \overline{B}^L _{m+1})\overline{B}^R_{n+1}

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.8
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{prop:calculate_Xi}, the morphism $K $ is given by \[ \underline{\beta}_0 (x) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (y) \mapsto \Big( \frac{1}{x}- \frac{1}{\underline{b}(x)} \Big) \Big( \frac{1}{\log^L y } - \frac{1}{\underline{b}(y)} \Big). \] Lemma \ref{lem:identify_primel} identifies the generating formal power series $\mathfrak{p}(S,T)$ for the primitive elements $p_i \otimes p_j$; thus the image of $\mathfrak{p}(S,T)$ is given by substituting the power series $x= \exp^L S $, $y=\exp^L T$ in the above exression (note that the left module structure of $MU_*MU$ is used), which gives \[ \mathfrak{p}(S,T) \mapsto \Big( \frac{1}{\exp^L S}- \frac{1}{\underline{b}(\exp^L S)} \Big) \Big( \frac{1}{\log^L ( \exp^L T)} - \frac{1}{\underline{b}(\exp^L T)} \Big). \] Simplifying and reversing the order in the two brackets, this gives: \[ \Big( \frac{1}{\exp^R S}- \frac{1}{\exp^L S} \Big) \Big( \frac{1}{\exp^R T} - \frac{1}{T} \Big). \] The result follows from the definition of $\mathfrak{p}(S,T)$ and of the reduced Bernoulli numbers.

nodes.statement_short: Substitute $x=\exp^L S$, $y=\exp^L T$ into the formula for $K$ (via Lemma 5.6) and simplify to Bernoulli generating series.
