nodes.label: eqn:q0_hol

nodes.name: Tate curve formal group law
nodes.statement: The composite $L \rightarrow {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [[q]][u]$ classifies the (graded) formal group law associated to the Tate Weierstrass curve defined over ${\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [[q]] [u]$.

nodes.name: Multiplicative reduction of the Tate curve formal group law
nodes.statement: After reduction $q \mapsto 0$, this is the multiplicative (graded) formal group law ${\mathbb{G}_{\mathrm{m}, u}}$ over ${\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [[q]][u]$, since the Tate curve has multiplicative reduction.

nodes.name: Formal group law of the Weierstrass curve
nodes.statement: The universal Weierstrass curve over the ring of holomorphic modular forms ${MF}$ is not an elliptic curve; however, the associated formal group law is defined, since the curve is smooth at the identity section. Similarly for the Tate curve.

nodes.name: Ring MF^mer of meromorphic modular forms
nodes.statement: The ring ${MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}$ of meromorphic modular forms over ${\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$ is isomorphic to $ {MF} [\Delta^{-1}]$, where $\Delta$ is the discriminant.

nodes.name: Constant term map q^0 on meromorphic forms
nodes.statement: The $q$-expansion of a meromorphic modular form lies in ${\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [[q]][q^{-1}]$ and $q^0$ defines an additive morphism $q^0 : {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [[q]][q^{-1}] \rightarrow {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$.

nodes.name: Commutative diagram with meromorphic forms (10)
nodes.statement: This gives the following commutative diagram \begin{eqnarray} \xymatrix{ L \ar[r] \ar[d]_{{\mathbb{G}_{\mathrm{m}, u}}} & {MF} \ar@{^(->}[r] \ar[d] & {MF}^{\mathrm{mer}} \ar[d] \\ {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [u^{\pm 1}] & {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [[q]][u] \ar@{^(->}[r] \ar[l]^{q^0} & {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [[q]][q^{-1},u^{\pm 1}], \ar@{-->}@/^2pc/[ll]^{q^0} } \end{eqnarray} in which the solid arrows are ring morphisms.

nodes.name: Formal group laws over MF and MF^mer (10)
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ L \ar[r] \ar[d]_{{\mathbb{G}_{\mathrm{m}, u}}} & {MF} \ar@{^(->}[r] \ar[d] & {MF}^{\mathrm{mer}} \ar[d] \\ {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [u^{\pm 1}] & {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [[q]][u] \ar@{^(->}[r] \ar[l]^{q^0} & {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [[q]][q^{-1},u^{\pm 1}], \ar@{-->}@/^2pc/[ll]^{q^0} }
nodes.label: eqn:mf-fgl

nodes.name: Elliptic homology Ell
nodes.statement: The morphisms $L \rightarrow {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [u^{\pm 1}] $ and $L \rightarrow {MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}$ are Landweber exact and correspond respectively to $KU_{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$ (which will be denoted here simply by $KU$) and a version of elliptic homology, denoted by ${Ell}$.

nodes.name: Ell_0 KU is Katz's ring of divided congruences
nodes.statement: \cite[Theorem 2.7]{laures}. The ring ${Ell} _ 0 KU$ is isomorphic to Katz's ring $\mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$ of divided congruences over ${\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$.
conclusions: \cite[Theorem 2.7]{laures}. The ring ${Ell} _ 0 KU$ is isomorphic to Katz's ring $\mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$ of divided congruences over ${\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$.

nodes.name: Structure of Ell_* KU
nodes.statement: \ \begin{enumerate} \item The ring ${Ell}_* KU $ is concentrated in even degree and is $2$-periodic. \item The ring ${Ell}_0 KU$ is a subring of ${Ell}_0 KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}\cong ({Ell}_* \otimes KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q})_0$ and identifies with the sub-${\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$-module of sums $\sum_i f_i $ of modular forms such that the Fourier expansion $\Sigma_i f_i(q)$ has coefficients in ${\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$; this is precisely the ring $\mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$ of divided congruences \cite{katz}. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: q^0 realized by a map of spectra Ell -> KU (Miller's elliptic character)
nodes.statement: The additive morphism $q^0 : {MF}^{\mathrm{mer}} \rightarrow {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [u^{\pm 1}]$ is realized by a morphism of spectra $q^0 : {Ell} \rightarrow KU$, which is derived from Miller's elliptic character (see \cite{laures}, following Miller \cite{millerW}).

nodes.name: Reduction map rho-bar^1
nodes.statement: Hence there is an induced morphism of spectra $ {Ell} \wedge {Ell} \rightarrow KU \wedge {Ell} , $ which induces a morphism of right ${Ell}_*$-modules \[ \overline{\rho}^1 : {Ell}_* {Ell} \rightarrow KU_* {Ell}, \] which is used in defining Laures' $f$-invariant \cite{laures} (see Section \ref{subsect:f_inv}).

nodes.name: Rational Landweber exact identifications
nodes.statement: Since ${Ell}$ and $KU$ are Landweber exact, ${Ell}_* {Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} \cong {Ell}_* \otimes {Ell}_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ and $KU_* {Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} \cong KU_*\otimes {Ell}_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}$.

nodes.name: Rationalized rho-bar^1 is q^0
nodes.statement: The morphism $\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ is the morphism of right ${Ell}_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}$-modules: \[ q^0 \otimes {Ell}_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} : {Ell}_* \otimes {Ell}_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} \cong {Ell}_* {Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} \rightarrow KU_* {Ell}\otimes \mathbb{Q} \cong KU_* \otimes {Ell}_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} \]
conclusions: The morphism $\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ is the morphism of right ${Ell}_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}$-modules: \[ q^0 \otimes {Ell}_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} : {Ell}_* \otimes {Ell}_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} \cong {Ell}_* {Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} \rightarrow KU_* {Ell}\otimes \mathbb{Q} \cong KU_* \otimes {Ell}_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} \]
nodes.label: prop:rho_rat

nodes.name: Morphism of short exact sequences for rho-bar^1
nodes.statement: There is a morphism of short exact sequences of right ${Ell}_*$-modules \begin{eqnarray} \xymatrix{ \ \ \ \ 0 \ar[r] & {Ell}_*{Ell} \ar[r] \ar[d]_{\overline{\rho}^1} & {Ell}_*{Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} \ar[r] \ar[d]^{\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes \mathbb{Q}} & {Ell}_*{Ell} \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} \ar[r] \ar[d]^{\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}} & 0 \\ 0 \ar[r] & KU_* {Ell} \ar[r] & KU_* {Ell}\otimes \mathbb{Q} \ar[r] & KU_* {Ell} \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} \ar[r] & 0. } \end{eqnarray}

nodes.name: Short exact sequences for rho-bar^1 (11)
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ \ \ \ \ 0 \ar[r] & {Ell}_*{Ell} \ar[r] \ar[d]_{\overline{\rho}^1} & {Ell}_*{Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} \ar[r] \ar[d]^{\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes \mathbb{Q}} & {Ell}_*{Ell} \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} \ar[r] \ar[d]^{\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}} & 0 \\ 0 \ar[r] & KU_* {Ell} \ar[r] & KU_* {Ell}\otimes \mathbb{Q} \ar[r] & KU_* {Ell} \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} \ar[r] & 0. }
nodes.label: eqn:ses-rho1

nodes.name: rho-bar^1 mod Q/Z determined by q^0
nodes.statement: Thus $\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$ is determined by $\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ and hence by the additive morphism $q^0$.

nodes.name: rho-bar^1 versus rho^1 in defining the f-invariant
nodes.statement: Following \cite[Theorem 4.2]{behrens_laures}, the morphism $\overline{\rho}^1$ is used here to define the $f$-invariant rather than the analogous morphism $\rho^1 : {Ell}_*{Ell} \rightarrow {Ell}_* KU$ (compare \cite[Proposition 3.9]{laures}). The relationship between the two approaches to calculating the $f$-invariant is explained by \cite[Proposition 3.10]{laures}.

nodes.name: Elliptic cocycle kappa_Ell
nodes.statement: Base change along $MU_* \rightarrow {Ell}_*$ gives a cocycle \[ \kappa_{{Ell}} :=\ _{{Ell}_*}\kappa _{{Ell}_*} \in \mathrm{Hom}_{{Ell}_*} ({Ell}_*(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) , {Ell}_* {Ell} \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [-4]), \] which represents a class $[\kappa_{{Ell}}] \in \mathrm{Ext}^1 _{{Ell}_*{Ell}} ({Ell}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0), {Ell}_* \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}}[-4])$, by Lemma \ref{lem:cocycle-base-change}.

nodes.name: kappa_Ell is the reduction of _{Ell}K_{Ell}
nodes.statement: The morphism $\kappa_{{Ell}}$ is the reduction of the morphism \[ _{{Ell}_*}K_{{Ell}_*} \in \mathrm{Hom}_{{Ell}_*} ({Ell}_*(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) , {Ell}_* {Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4]) \] via the morphism ${Ell}_* {Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4] \twoheadrightarrow {Ell}_* {Ell}\otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [-4]$.
conclusions: The morphism $\kappa_{{Ell}}$ is the reduction of the morphism \[ _{{Ell}_*}K_{{Ell}_*} \in \mathrm{Hom}_{{Ell}_*} ({Ell}_*(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) , {Ell}_* {Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4]) \] via the morphism ${Ell}_* {Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4] \twoheadrightarrow {Ell}_* {Ell}\otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [-4]$.
nodes.label: lem:kappa_ell_Xi

nodes.name: Reduction of kappa_Ell along rho-bar^1
nodes.statement: The morphism of right ${Ell}_*$-modules \[ (\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} ) \circ \kappa_{Ell} \in \mathrm{Hom} ({Ell}_*(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) , KU_* {Ell} \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [-4]) \] coincides with the morphism $_{KU_*} \kappa _{{Ell}_*}$. Hence, the morphism $(\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} ) \circ \kappa_{Ell}$ is the reduction of the morphism of right ${Ell}_*$-modules \[_{KU_*}K_{{Ell}_*} \in \mathrm{Hom} ({Ell}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) , KU_* {Ell}\otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4]) \] via the morphism $KU_* {Ell}\otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4] \twoheadrightarrow KU_* {Ell} \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [-4]$.
nodes.statement_short: $\overline\rho^1\circ\kappa_{Ell}$ equals ${}_{KU_*}\kappa_{Ell_*}$, hence is the reduction of ${}_{KU_*}K_{Ell_*}$.
conclusions: The morphism of right ${Ell}_*$-modules \[ (\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} ) \circ \kappa_{Ell} \in \mathrm{Hom} ({Ell}_*(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) , KU_* {Ell} \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [-4]) \] coincides with the morphism $_{KU_*} \kappa _{{Ell}_*}$

Hence, the morphism $(\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} ) \circ \kappa_{Ell}$ is the reduction of the morphism of right ${Ell}_*$-modules \[_{KU_*}K_{{Ell}_*} \in \mathrm{Hom} ({Ell}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) , KU_* {Ell}\otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4]) \] via the morphism $KU_* {Ell}\otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4] \twoheadrightarrow KU_* {Ell} \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [-4]$.
nodes.label: prop:kappa-tmf

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.7
nodes.statement: The diagram of short exact sequences (\ref{eqn:ses-rho1}) together with Lemma \ref{lem:kappa_ell_Xi} show that it is sufficient to calculate the respective morphisms to $KU_* {Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q}$. This can be carried out using the identification of $\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ given by Proposition \ref{prop:rho_rat}. There is a commutative diagram \[ \xymatrix{ {Ell}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar@/^1pc/[rd]^{_{{Ell}_*}K_{{Ell}_*}} \ar[d]_{_{{MF}}K_{{Ell}_*}} \\ {MF} \otimes_{MU_*} MU_*{Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4] \ar[d]_{q^0 \otimes {Ell}_*} \ar[r] & {Ell}_* \otimes _{MU_*} MU_* {Ell}_*\otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4] \ar@/^1pc/[ld]^(.4){\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes \mathbb{Q}} \\ KU_* {Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4], } \] where the horizontal morphism is induced by ${MF} \rightarrow {MF}^{\mathrm{mer}} \cong {Ell}_*$. The commutativity of the top triangle follows from the fact that the elliptic formal group law is defined over the ring of holomorphic modular forms, ${MF}$, and the commutativity of the lower triangle follows from the commutative diagram (\ref{eqn:mf-fgl}). To complete the proof, observe that the vertical composite is the morphism $_{KU_*}K_{{Ell}_*}$, by the commutative diagram (\ref{eqn:q0_hol}).
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to rational targets via diagram (11) and Lemma 6.6; then use that the elliptic formal group law is defined over $MF$ and diagrams (9), (10).

nodes.name: Reduce to rational targets
nodes.statement: The diagram of short exact sequences (\ref{eqn:ses-rho1}) together with Lemma \ref{lem:kappa_ell_Xi} show that it is sufficient to calculate the respective morphisms to $KU_* {Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q}$. This can be carried out using the identification of $\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ given by Proposition \ref{prop:rho_rat}.
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to compare the maps to $KU_*Ell\otimes\mathbb{Q}$, using Proposition 6.4.

nodes.name: Factor through MF
nodes.statement: There is a commutative diagram \[ \xymatrix{ {Ell}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar@/^1pc/[rd]^{_{{Ell}_*}K_{{Ell}_*}} \ar[d]_{_{{MF}}K_{{Ell}_*}} \\ {MF} \otimes_{MU_*} MU_*{Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4] \ar[d]_{q^0 \otimes {Ell}_*} \ar[r] & {Ell}_* \otimes _{MU_*} MU_* {Ell}_*\otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4] \ar@/^1pc/[ld]^(.4){\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes \mathbb{Q}} \\ KU_* {Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4], } \] where the horizontal morphism is induced by ${MF} \rightarrow {MF}^{\mathrm{mer}} \cong {Ell}_*$. The commutativity of the top triangle follows from the fact that the elliptic formal group law is defined over the ring of holomorphic modular forms, ${MF}$, and the commutativity of the lower triangle follows from the commutative diagram (\ref{eqn:mf-fgl}).
nodes.statement_short: Factor through $MF$; triangles commute by the holomorphic formal group law and diagram (10).

nodes.name: Identify the composite
nodes.statement: To complete the proof, observe that the vertical composite is the morphism $_{KU_*}K_{{Ell}_*}$, by the commutative diagram (\ref{eqn:q0_hol}).
nodes.statement_short: The vertical composite is ${}_{KU_*}K_{Ell_*}$ by diagram (9).

nodes.name: f-invariant of Laures
nodes.statement: The $f$-invariant of Laures \cite{laures} is a homomorphism \[ f : \pi_{2k}(S) \otimes {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} \rightarrow \mathfrak{D} _{\mathbb{Q}} / \Big( \mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} + ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_0)_{\mathbb{Q}} + ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_{k+1})_{\mathbb{Q}} \Big). \]

nodes.name: Invariant iota^2
nodes.statement: This factorizes across an invariant \[ \iota^2 : \mathrm{Ext}^{2,2k+2} _{MU_*MU} (MU_* , MU_*) \otimes {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} \hookrightarrow \mathfrak{D} _{\mathbb{Q}} / \Big(\mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_0)_{\mathbb{Q}} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_{k+1})_{\mathbb{Q}} \Big), \] where the injectivity is given by \cite[Proposition 3.9]{laures}.

nodes.name: iota^2 on Ext^1 via the chromatic connecting map
nodes.statement: Via the chromatic connecting map \[ \mathrm{Ext}^{1,*}_{MU_*MU} (MU_*,MU_* \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} ) \stackrel{\partial_1}{\rightarrow} \mathrm{Ext}^{2,*}_{MU_*MU} (MU_*,MU_* ) \otimes {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}, \] $\iota^2$ defines an invariant of $ \mathrm{Ext}^{1,*}_{MU_*MU} (MU_*,MU_* \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} ). $

nodes.name: Cobar complex M_k of Ell
nodes.statement: Write $M_k ^{\bullet +1} \cong \pi_{2k} ({Ell}^{\bullet +1})$ for the cobar complex associated to ${Ell}$.

nodes.name: Behrens-Laures morphism of semi-cosimplicial groups
nodes.statement: A morphism between semi-cosimplical abelian groups is defined \cite[page 25]{behrens_laures}: \begin{eqnarray} \xymatrix{ M_k^{(1)} \ar@<.5ex>[r]|{d_0} \ar@<-.5ex>[r]|{d_1} \ar[d] _{\overline{\rho}^0} & M_k^{(2)} \ar@<1ex>[rr]|{d_0} \ar@<0ex>[rr]|{d_1} \ar@<-1ex>[rr]|{d_2} \ar[d] _{\overline{\rho}^1} && M_k^{(3)} \ar[d] \ar[d] _{\overline{\rho}^2} \\ ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_k)_{{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}} \ar@<.5ex>[r]|(.6){d_0} \ar@<-.5ex>[r]|(.6){d_1} & \mathfrak{D}_{{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}} \ar@<1ex>[rr]|(.3){d_0} \ar@<0ex>[rr]|(.3){d_1} \ar@<-1ex>[rr]|(.3){d_2} && \mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Q}} / \big( ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_k)_{\mathbb{Q}} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_0)_{\mathbb{Q}} \big) } \end{eqnarray}

nodes.name: Behrens-Laures semi-cosimplicial morphism (12)
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ M_k^{(1)} \ar@<.5ex>[r]|{d_0} \ar@<-.5ex>[r]|{d_1} \ar[d] _{\overline{\rho}^0} & M_k^{(2)} \ar@<1ex>[rr]|{d_0} \ar@<0ex>[rr]|{d_1} \ar@<-1ex>[rr]|{d_2} \ar[d] _{\overline{\rho}^1} && M_k^{(3)} \ar[d] \ar[d] _{\overline{\rho}^2} \\ ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_k)_{{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}} \ar@<.5ex>[r]|(.6){d_0} \ar@<-.5ex>[r]|(.6){d_1} & \mathfrak{D}_{{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}} \ar@<1ex>[rr]|(.3){d_0} \ar@<0ex>[rr]|(.3){d_1} \ar@<-1ex>[rr]|(.3){d_2} && \mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Q}} / \big( ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_k)_{\mathbb{Q}} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_0)_{\mathbb{Q}} \big) }
nodes.label: eqn:BL_semicosimplicial

nodes.name: iota^2 induced by rho-bar^2
nodes.statement: The composite of $\overline{\rho}^2$ with the projection \[ \mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Q}} / \big( ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_k)_{\mathbb{Q}} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_0)_{\mathbb{Q}} \big) \twoheadrightarrow \mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Q}} / \big( \mathfrak{D}_{{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_k)_{\mathbb{Q}} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_0)_{\mathbb{Q}} \big) \] induces the morphism \[ \iota^2 : \mathrm{Ext}^{2,2k} _{{Ell}_*{Ell}} ({Ell}_* , {Ell}_*) \otimes {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} \hookrightarrow \mathfrak{D} _{\mathbb{Q}} / \Big(\mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_0)_{\mathbb{Q}} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_{k})_{\mathbb{Q}} \Big), \] on restriction to cocycles.

nodes.name: Cobar chain cocomplex differentials delta
nodes.statement: Write the chain cocomplex associated to the cobar complex as \[ \xymatrix{ M_k^{(1)} \ar[r]^{\delta^0} & M_k^{(2)} \ar[r]^{\delta^1} & M_k^{(3)} \ar[r] & \ldots \ \ . } \]

nodes.name: iota^2 via rho-bar^1 of a rational coboundary
nodes.statement: Let $x$ be a $2$-cocycle in $M_k^{(2)}$ which represents a class $$[x] \in \mathrm{Ext}^{2, *} _{{Ell}_* {Ell}} ({Ell}_*, {Ell}_*).$$ Then \begin{enumerate} \item there exists an element $c \in M_k^{(1)}$ and an integer $n$ such that $\delta^1 c = nx$; \item the invariant $\iota^2 [x]$ is represented by the element $\frac{1}{n}\overline{\rho}^1 (c) \in \mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Q}}$. \end{enumerate}
assumptions: $x$ be a $2$-cocycle in $M_k^{(2)}$ which represents a class $$[x] \in \mathrm{Ext}^{2, *} _{{Ell}_* {Ell}} ({Ell}_*, {Ell}_*).$$
conclusions: there exists an element $c \in M_k^{(1)}$ and an integer $n$ such that $\delta^1 c = nx$
the invariant $\iota^2 [x]$ is represented by the element $\frac{1}{n}\overline{\rho}^1 (c) \in \mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Q}}$
nodes.label: lem:iota2_rho1

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.1
nodes.statement: A straightforward consequence of the commutative diagram (\ref{eqn:BL_semicosimplicial}) together with the fact that $\mathrm{Ext}^d_{{Ell}_*{Ell}}({Ell}_* , {Ell}_*) \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ is trivial for $d >0$.
nodes.statement_short: From diagram (12) and rational vanishing of positive-degree Ext.

nodes.name: f-invariant of the boundary of a 1-cocycle
nodes.statement: Let $[c] \in \mathrm{Ext}^{1,2k}_{{Ell}_*{Ell}} ({Ell}_* , {Ell}_* \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]})$ be represented by a cocycle $c : {Ell}_* [2k] \rightarrow {Ell}_* {Ell} \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$ which factorizes as left ${Ell}_*$-module morphisms \[ \xymatrix{ {Ell}_*[2k] \ar[r]^(.4){\hat{c}} \ar[rd] _c & {Ell}_*{Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} \ar@{->>}[d] \\ & {Ell}_*{Ell} \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}. } \] Then the invariant $\iota^2( \partial_1 [c])$ is represented by the image of the generator under the map \[ \xymatrix{ {Ell}_*[2k] \ar[rr]^(.45){\ _{KU_*} \hat{c} _{{Ell}_*} } && KU_*{Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q}, } \] where $KU_{2k} {Ell}\otimes \mathbb{Q}$ is identified with $\mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Q}}$ by periodicity.
assumptions: $[c] \in \mathrm{Ext}^{1,2k}_{{Ell}_*{Ell}} ({Ell}_* , {Ell}_* \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]})$ be represented by a cocycle $c : {Ell}_* [2k] \rightarrow {Ell}_* {Ell} \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$ which factorizes as left ${Ell}_*$-module morphisms \[ \xymatrix{ {Ell}_*[2k] \ar[r]^(.4){\hat{c}} \ar[rd] _c & {Ell}_*{Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} \ar@{->>}[d] \\ & {Ell}_*{Ell} \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}. } \]
conclusions: the invariant $\iota^2( \partial_1 [c])$ is represented by the image of the generator under the map \[ \xymatrix{ {Ell}_*[2k] \ar[rr]^(.45){\ _{KU_*} \hat{c} _{{Ell}_*} } && KU_*{Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q}, } \] where $KU_{2k} {Ell}\otimes \mathbb{Q}$ is identified with $\mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Q}}$ by periodicity.
nodes.label: prop:f-inv_1cocycle

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 7.2
nodes.statement: The result follows from Lemma \ref{lem:iota2_rho1}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 7.1.

nodes.name: f-invariant of a primitive
nodes.statement: For $\mathfrak{p}$ a primitive in $\mathbf{P} MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$, let $f(\mathfrak{p})$ denote the $f$-invariant of $ \mathfrak{p}^* [\kappa]\in \mathrm{Ext}^1_{MU_*MU} (MU_*[|\mathfrak{p}| +4] , MU_* \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]})$.

nodes.name: Reduced Bernoulli numbers of Ell and KU
nodes.statement: For $n$ a natural number, write $\overline{B}_n ^{{Ell}}\in {Ell}_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ (respectively $\overline{B}_n ^{KU} \in KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}$) for the reduced Bernoulli numbers associated to the complex orientations of ${Ell}$ and $KU$ respectively.

nodes.name: Bernoulli numbers of Ell are holomorphic modular forms
nodes.statement: The reduced Bernoulli number $\overline{B}_n ^{{Ell}}$ is defined in the ring ${MF} \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ of holomorphic modular forms, since the formal group law of ${Ell}_*$ is the image of a formal group law over ${MF}$ via the morphism ${MF}\hookrightarrow {MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}\cong {Ell}_*$.

nodes.name: f-invariant of p_s tensor p_t
nodes.statement: Let $s,t$ be natural numbers. The $f$-invariant $$f(p_s \otimes p_t) \in \mathfrak{D} _{\mathbb{Q}} / \Big(\mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_0)_{\mathbb{Q}} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_{s+t+2})_{\mathbb{Q}} \Big),$$ is represented by the element $ - \overline{B}_{t+1}^{Ell} \overline{B} _{s+1} ^{KU} \in \mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Q}}. $
nodes.statement_short: $f(p_s\otimes p_t)$ is represented by $-\overline B^{Ell}_{t+1}\overline B^{KU}_{s+1}$.
assumptions: $s,t$ be natural numbers
conclusions: The $f$-invariant $$f(p_s \otimes p_t) \in \mathfrak{D} _{\mathbb{Q}} / \Big(\mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_0)_{\mathbb{Q}} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_{s+t+2})_{\mathbb{Q}} \Big),$$ is represented by the element $ - \overline{B}_{t+1}^{Ell} \overline{B} _{s+1} ^{KU} \in \mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Q}}. $
nodes.label: thm:f-pspt

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 7.5
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{prop:f-inv_1cocycle}, these invariants are represented by the morphism $ \ _{KU_*} ( K \circ \mathfrak{p}) _{{Ell}_*}. $ Hence, by Proposition \ref{prop:restrict_Xi_prim}, $f(p_s \otimes p_t)$ is represented by \[ (\overline{B}_{s+1} ^{{Ell}} - \overline{B} _{s+1} ^{KU}) \overline{B}_{t+1}^{{Ell}} \in \mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Q}}. \] The term $\overline{B}_{s+1}^{{Ell}} \overline{B}_{t+1} ^{{Ell}}$ becomes zero on passage to the quotient, since it belongs to the subgroup $({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_{s+t+2})_{\mathbb{Q}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 7.2 reduces to ${}_{KU_*}(K\circ\mathfrak p)_{Ell_*}$, Proposition 5.8 evaluates it, and the $Ell\cdot Ell$ term dies in the quotient.

nodes.name: Reduce to K
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{prop:f-inv_1cocycle}, these invariants are represented by the morphism $ \ _{KU_*} ( K \circ \mathfrak{p}) _{{Ell}_*}. $
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 7.2 represents the invariant by $K\circ\mathfrak p$ base-changed.

nodes.name: Evaluate on primitives
nodes.statement: Hence, by Proposition \ref{prop:restrict_Xi_prim}, $f(p_s \otimes p_t)$ is represented by \[ (\overline{B}_{s+1} ^{{Ell}} - \overline{B} _{s+1} ^{KU}) \overline{B}_{t+1}^{{Ell}} \in \mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Q}}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 5.8 gives the representing element.

nodes.name: Kill the Ell-Ell term
nodes.statement: The term $\overline{B}_{s+1}^{{Ell}} \overline{B}_{t+1} ^{{Ell}}$ becomes zero on passage to the quotient, since it belongs to the subgroup $({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_{s+t+2})_{\mathbb{Q}}$.
nodes.statement_short: The $Ell\cdot Ell$ product is a meromorphic modular form, zero in the quotient.

nodes.name: Symmetric form of the f-invariant of p_s tensor p_t
nodes.statement: Let $s,t$ be natural numbers. The invariant $f(p_s \otimes p_t)$ is represented by the element $ \overline{B}_{s+1}^{Ell} \overline{B} _{t+1} ^{KU} \in \mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Q}}. $
assumptions: $s,t$ be natural numbers
conclusions: The invariant $f(p_s \otimes p_t)$ is represented by the element $ \overline{B}_{s+1}^{Ell} \overline{B} _{t+1} ^{KU} \in \mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Q}}. $
nodes.label: cor:symm_f-invariant

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 7.6
nodes.statement: The group $\mathfrak{S}_2$ acts on $MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ by comodule morphisms induced by interchanging the factors $\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0$. It is straightforward to show that the induced right action on $\mathrm{Ext}_{MU_*MU} ^2 (MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) , MU_* [-4]) $ satisfies \[ ([e_\tau]^2 ) \sigma = \mathrm{sgn} (\sigma) [e_\tau]^2. \] Hence $ f (p_s \otimes p_t) = - f (p_t \otimes p_s); $ in particular, the $f$-invariant of $p_s \otimes p_t$ is represented by the element $\overline{B}_{s+1}^{Ell} \overline{B} _{t+1} ^{KU}$.
nodes.statement_short: The swap of factors acts on $[e_\tau]^2$ by the sign, so $f(p_s\otimes p_t)=-f(p_t\otimes p_s)$; combine with Theorem 7.5.

nodes.name: Swap action
nodes.statement: The group $\mathfrak{S}_2$ acts on $MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ by comodule morphisms induced by interchanging the factors $\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the $\mathfrak S_2$ action swapping factors.

nodes.name: Sign of the double transfer
nodes.statement: It is straightforward to show that the induced right action on $\mathrm{Ext}_{MU_*MU} ^2 (MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) , MU_* [-4]) $ satisfies \[ ([e_\tau]^2 ) \sigma = \mathrm{sgn} (\sigma) [e_\tau]^2. \]
nodes.statement_short: The double transfer transforms by the sign.

nodes.name: Antisymmetry
nodes.statement: Hence $ f (p_s \otimes p_t) = - f (p_t \otimes p_s); $ in particular, the $f$-invariant of $p_s \otimes p_t$ is represented by the element $\overline{B}_{s+1}^{Ell} \overline{B} _{t+1} ^{KU}$.
nodes.statement_short: Antisymmetry of $f$ and Theorem 7.5 give the formula.

nodes.name: f'-invariant of Behrens
nodes.statement: For $p \geq 5$ a prime, Behrens \cite{behrens} defines the $f'$-invariant via a morphism \[ f' : \mathrm{Ext}^{2,2k+2} _{MU_*MU} (MU_* , MU_*)_{(p)} \rightarrow H^0(C (l)^\bullet/p^\infty, v_1 ^\infty )_{2k+2}, \] where $l$ is a topological generator of $\mathbb{Z}_p^\times$ (for example $l = \gamma$) and $C(l)^\bullet$ is an explicit semi-cosimplicial abelian group which is defined in terms of modular forms of level one and modular forms of level $l$.

nodes.name: Modular forms of level Gamma_0(l)
nodes.statement: Namely, as in \cite{behrens}, write $M_k (\Gamma_0 (l))_{\mathbb{Z}_p}$ for the space of modular forms of weight $k$ and level $\Gamma_0(l)$ over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ which are meromorphic at the cusps.

nodes.name: Semi-cosimplicial group C(l)
nodes.statement: Then the semi-cosimplicial graded abelian group is of the form \[ C(l)^\bullet_{2k} = \Big( \xymatrix{ (M_k)_{\mathbb{Z}_p} \ar@<.5ex>[r]|(.4){d_0} \ar@<-.5ex>[r]|(.4){d_1} & *{ \begin{array}{c} M_k(\Gamma_0 (l))_{\mathbb{Z}_p}\\ \times\\ (M_k)_{\mathbb{Z}_p} \end{array} } \ar@<1ex>[r] \ar[r] \ar@<-1ex>[r] & M_k(\Gamma_0 (l))_{\mathbb{Z}_p} } \Big), \] where the morphisms $d_0, d_1$ are identified explicitly in terms of $q$-expansions.

nodes.name: p-local BP conventions of Behrens and Laures
nodes.statement: Behrens and Laures work $p$-locally and replace $MU$ by $BP$, so as to accord better with the results of Miller, Ravenel and Wilson \cite{MRW}. Thus, below ${Ell}_*$ denotes $p$-local elliptic homology ($p \geq 5$), and a $p$-typical orientation $BP_* \rightarrow {Ell}_*$ is fixed, as in \cite{behrens_laures}.

nodes.name: Behrens-Laures diagram for the f'-invariant
nodes.statement: Behrens and Laures shows that the $f'$-invariant fits into a commutative diagram \begin{eqnarray} \xymatrix{ \mathrm{Ext}^{2,4t}_{BP_*BP} (BP_*, BP_*) \ar[dd]_{f'} & \mathrm{Ext}^{0,4t}_{BP_*BP} (BP_*, BP_*/p^\infty,v_1^\infty) \ar[l]_{\partial_1\partial_2} \ar[d]^{L_{v_2}} \ar@/_1pc/[ldd] \\ &\mathrm{Ext}^{0,4t}_{BP_*BP} (BP_*, BP_*/p^\infty,v_1^\infty [v_2^{-1}]) \ar[d]^\cong \\ H^0(C (l)^\bullet/p^\infty, v_1 ^\infty )_{4t} & \mathrm{Ext}^{0,4t}_{{Ell}_*{Ell}} ({Ell}_*, {Ell}_*/p^\infty,v_1^\infty), \ar[l]^(.55){\cong}_(.55){\tilde{\eta}} } \end{eqnarray} where the diagonal arrow is induced by the $p$-typical orientation of ${Ell}$, the vertical change of rings isomorphism is given in the proof of \cite[Lemma 4.6]{behrens_laures} and the isomorphism $\tilde{\eta}$ in \cite[Proposition 3.17]{behrens_laures}. The upper triangle is commutative by \cite[Diagram 3.15]{behrens_laures} and the lower triangle is commutative by \cite[Diagram 3.16]{behrens_laures}.
nodes.statement_short: $f'$ factors through $\partial_1\partial_2$ from $\mathrm{Ext}^0(BP_*/p^\infty,v_1^\infty)$ and Ell-comodule primitives via the isomorphism $\tilde\eta$.

nodes.name: f'-invariant diagram (13)
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ \mathrm{Ext}^{2,4t}_{BP_*BP} (BP_*, BP_*) \ar[dd]_{f'} & \mathrm{Ext}^{0,4t}_{BP_*BP} (BP_*, BP_*/p^\infty,v_1^\infty) \ar[l]_{\partial_1\partial_2} \ar[d]^{L_{v_2}} \ar@/_1pc/[ldd] \\ &\mathrm{Ext}^{0,4t}_{BP_*BP} (BP_*, BP_*/p^\infty,v_1^\infty [v_2^{-1}]) \ar[d]^\cong \\ H^0(C (l)^\bullet/p^\infty, v_1 ^\infty )_{4t} & \mathrm{Ext}^{0,4t}_{{Ell}_*{Ell}} ({Ell}_*, {Ell}_*/p^\infty,v_1^\infty), \ar[l]^(.55){\cong}_(.55){\tilde{\eta}} }
nodes.label: eqn:f'_invariant

nodes.name: Double transfer factorization in BP-Ext
nodes.statement: Recall that $\overline{\Theta}$ defines a chromatic factorization of the double transfer and this induces a commutative diagram \begin{eqnarray} \xymatrix{ & \mathrm{Ext}_{BP_*BP}^{0,*-4} (BP_* , BP_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)) \ar[d]^{BP_* (\overline{\Theta})} \ar[ld] \\ \mathrm{Ext}^{2,*}_{BP_* BP} (BP_* , BP_*) & \mathrm{Ext}^{0,*}_{BP_* BP} (BP_* , BP_* /p^\infty, v_1^\infty) \ar[l]^{\partial_1 \partial_2}, } \end{eqnarray} by Proposition \ref{prop:kappa-transfer} and Proposition \ref{prop:second-factorization} (with $BP$ in place of $MU$).

nodes.name: Algebraic double transfer via Theta-bar (14)
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ & \mathrm{Ext}_{BP_*BP}^{0,*-4} (BP_* , BP_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)) \ar[d]^{BP_* (\overline{\Theta})} \ar[ld] \\ \mathrm{Ext}^{2,*}_{BP_* BP} (BP_* , BP_*) & \mathrm{Ext}^{0,*}_{BP_* BP} (BP_* , BP_* /p^\infty, v_1^\infty) \ar[l]^{\partial_1 \partial_2}, }
nodes.label: eqn:alg_double_transfer

nodes.name: Independence of the choice of Theta-bar
nodes.statement: The composite morphism \[ \xymatrix{ \mathrm{Ext}_{BP_*BP}^{0,4t -4} (BP_* , BP_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) ) \ar[rr]^{BP_* (\overline{\Theta})} && \mathrm{Ext}^{0,4t}_{BP_* BP} (BP_* , BP_* /p^\infty, v_1^\infty) \ar[d] \\ && \mathrm{Ext}^{0,4t}_{{Ell}_*{Ell}} ({Ell}_*, {Ell}_*/p^\infty,v_1^\infty) } \] induced by the change of rings associated to the $p$-typical orientation $BP_* \rightarrow {Ell}_*$, is independent of the choice of $\overline{\Theta}$.
conclusions: is independent of the choice of $\overline{\Theta}$.
nodes.label: lem:independence_Theta

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.8
nodes.statement: Follows from the commutativity of the diagrams (\ref{eqn:f'_invariant}) and (\ref{eqn:alg_double_transfer}), together with the fact that the bottom horizontal morphism in (\ref{eqn:f'_invariant}) is an isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Commutativity of diagrams (13) and (14) with the isomorphism $\tilde\eta$.

nodes.name: f'-invariant for primitive elements
nodes.statement: By naturality, it suffices to replace the composite morphism considered above by the morphism \[ {Ell}_* (\overline{\Theta}) : \mathrm{Ext}_{{Ell}_*{Ell}}^{0,4t -4} ({Ell}_* , {Ell}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) ) \rightarrow \mathrm{Ext}_{{Ell}_*{Ell}}^{0,4t} ({Ell}_* , {Ell}_* /p^\infty,v_1^\infty ) \] which is considered as being the $f'$ invariant for primitive elements.

nodes.name: Diagram for f' via theta
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{thm:MU-thetas} gives a commutative diagram \[ \xymatrix{ & \mathbf{P} {Ell}_*(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar@{^(.>}[d] \ar@/^1pc/@<4em>@{.>}[dd]^{f'} \ar@/^3pc/@<4em>@{.>}[ddd]^{f''} \\ {Ell}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar[dd]_{{Ell}_* (\theta)} & {Ell}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar@{.>}[l]_{\sigma'} \ar[d]^{{Ell}_*(\overline{\Theta})} \\ & {Ell}_* /p^\infty, v_1 ^\infty [-4] \ar@{^(->}[d] \\ {Ell}_*KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}[-4] \ar[r] & {Ell}_* KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}/\Big({Ell}_*KU _{(p)} \oplus ({Ell}_*)_{\mathbb{Q}} \Big) [-4], } \] where the solid arrows denote comodule morphisms and the dotted arrows morphisms of $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$-modules.

nodes.name: Composite f''
nodes.statement: The composite of $f'$ with the monomorphism ${Ell}_* /p^\infty, v_1 ^\infty [-4] \hookrightarrow {Ell}_* KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}/\Big({Ell}_*KU _{(p)} \oplus ({Ell}_*)_{\mathbb{Q}} \Big) [-4]$ is denoted $f''$, as indicated.

nodes.name: Integrality of Ell_*(theta) after psi^gamma - 1
nodes.statement: The morphism ${Ell}_* (\theta)$ composed with the morphism induced by $\psi^\gamma - 1$ is integral in the appropriate sense, as a consequence of the construction of $\theta$. This can be related to the analysis of $H^0 (C(l)^\bullet/ p^\infty, v_1^\infty) $ using the identifications of \cite[Proposition 6.1]{behrens}.

nodes.name: Formula for Ell_*(theta) o sigma'
nodes.statement: The morphism ${Ell}_*(\theta) \circ \sigma'$ is given by Proposition \ref{prop:MUtheta_sigmap}, after base change to ${Ell}_*$; it is determined by $ \underline{\beta}_0 (x) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (y) \mapsto $ \[ \Big( \frac{1}{\underline{b}'(x) } - \frac{1}{x}\Big) \Big(\frac{1}{\log^{{Ell}} y} - \frac{1}{\underline{b}' (y) }\Big) + \sum _{i, j >0}\frac{B_i^{KU}}{i!}\frac{B_j^{KU}}{j!} \left( \frac{\gamma^i -1}{\gamma^{i+j}-1} \right) (\log^{Ell} x)^{i-1}(\log ^{Ell} y) ^{j-1}, \] where the power series $\underline{b}'$ is understood as $\exp^{KU} \circ \log^{Ell}$ when considered as a power series over ${Ell}_* KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}$.

nodes.name: f'-invariant of p_s tensor p_t
nodes.statement: The $f'$-invariant on the primitives of ${Ell}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) $ is determined by \[ f'' (p_s \otimes p_t) = \Big[ \overline{B}^{Ell}_{s+1}\overline{B}^{KU} _{t+1} + \overline{B}^{KU}_{s+1}\overline{B}^{KU} _{t+1}\frac{\gamma^{s+1}(1- \gamma^{t+1}) }{\gamma^{s+t+2}-1} \Big], \] where $s, t$ are natural numbers and $ \overline{B}^{Ell}_{s+1}\overline{B}^{KU} _{t+1} + \overline{B}^{KU}_{s+1}\overline{B}^{KU} _{t+1}\frac{\gamma^{s+1}(1- \gamma^{t+1}) }{\gamma^{s+t+2}-1} $ is considered as an element of ${Ell}_*KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}$.
nodes.statement_short: $f''(p_s\otimes p_t)$ is the class of $\overline B^{Ell}_{s+1}\overline B^{KU}_{t+1}+\overline B^{KU}_{s+1}\overline B^{KU}_{t+1}\gamma^{s+1}(1-\gamma^{t+1})/(\gamma^{s+t+2}-1)$.
assumptions: $s, t$ are natural numbers
conclusions: The $f'$-invariant on the primitives of ${Ell}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) $ is determined by \[ f'' (p_s \otimes p_t) = \Big[ \overline{B}^{Ell}_{s+1}\overline{B}^{KU} _{t+1} + \overline{B}^{KU}_{s+1}\overline{B}^{KU} _{t+1}\frac{\gamma^{s+1}(1- \gamma^{t+1}) }{\gamma^{s+t+2}-1} \Big], \]
nodes.label: thm:fprime

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 7.10
nodes.statement: The method of proof is similar to that used in Proposition \ref{prop:restrict_Xi_prim}. Substitute $x= \exp^{Ell} S$ and $y = \exp^{Ell} T$ in the power series representing ${Ell}_* (\theta) \circ \sigma'$; this gives the power series \[ \Big( \frac{1}{\exp^{KU} S} - \frac{1}{\exp^{Ell} S }\Big) \Big(\frac{1}{T} - \frac{1}{\exp^{KU} T }\Big) + \sum _{i, j >0}\frac{B_i^{KU}}{i!}\frac{B_j^{KU}}{j!} \left( \frac{\gamma^i -1}{\gamma^{i+j}-1} \right) S^{i-1}T ^{j-1}. \] The result follows by identifying coefficients.
nodes.statement_short: As for Proposition 5.8: substitute $x=\exp^{Ell}S$, $y=\exp^{Ell}T$ in the series for $Ell_*(\theta)\circ\sigma'$ and compare coefficients.

nodes.name: Method
nodes.statement: The method of proof is similar to that used in Proposition \ref{prop:restrict_Xi_prim}.
nodes.statement_short: Same method as Proposition 5.8.

nodes.name: Substitute exponentials
nodes.statement: Substitute $x= \exp^{Ell} S$ and $y = \exp^{Ell} T$ in the power series representing ${Ell}_* (\theta) \circ \sigma'$; this gives the power series \[ \Big( \frac{1}{\exp^{KU} S} - \frac{1}{\exp^{Ell} S }\Big) \Big(\frac{1}{T} - \frac{1}{\exp^{KU} T }\Big) + \sum _{i, j >0}\frac{B_i^{KU}}{i!}\frac{B_j^{KU}}{j!} \left( \frac{\gamma^i -1}{\gamma^{i+j}-1} \right) S^{i-1}T ^{j-1}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Substitute $\exp^{Ell}$ into the series for $Ell_*(\theta)\circ\sigma'$.

nodes.name: Identify coefficients
nodes.statement: The result follows by identifying coefficients.
nodes.statement_short: Read off the coefficients.

nodes.name: Relation between f and f' on double transfer classes
nodes.statement: The relationship between the $f$ and the $f'$ invariants (in the general case) is made explicit in \cite[Theorem 4.2]{behrens_laures} by analysing the semi-cosimplicial diagram (\ref{eqn:BL_semicosimplicial}). Upon restricting to classes arising from comodule primitives via the algebraic double transfer, the relationship is clear. Observe that Theorem \ref{thm:f-pspt}, Corollary \ref{cor:symm_f-invariant} and Theorem \ref{thm:fprime} show that, on passage to the quotient $$\mathfrak{D} _{\mathbb{Q}} / \Big(\mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_0)_{\mathbb{Q}} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_{s+t+2})_{\mathbb{Q}} \Big)$$ the elements $f(p_s \otimes p_t)$ and $f'(p_s \otimes p_t)$ both are defined by the class of the element $\overline{B}^{Ell}_{s+1}\overline{B}^{KU} _{t+1} $ in $\mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Q}}$, since the additional term appearing in Theorem \ref{thm:fprime} becomes trivial in this quotient. The relationship can be seen as a direct consequence of Lemma \ref{lem:restrict_Theta} and Corollary \ref{cor:relate_MUtheta}; here, the sign appearing in the leading term in Corollary \ref{cor:relate_MUtheta} has been avoided by following Behrens and Lawson in defining the $f$-invariant by using the morphism $\overline{\rho}^1$.
nodes.statement_short: On double-transfer classes of primitives, $f$ and $f'$ agree in the common quotient: both are the class of $\overline B^{Ell}_{s+1}\overline B^{KU}_{t+1}$.
nodes.label: rem:relate_f,f'

nodes.name: Comodule categories and structure morphism psi_M
nodes.statement: For $(A,\Gamma)$ a Hopf algebroid, the category of left $\Gamma$-comodules is denoted here $\Gamma \hspace{-.2em}-\hspace{-.2em} \mathrm{Comod}$ and the category of $A$-modules $A\hspace{-.2em}-\hspace{-.2em} \mathrm{Mod}$; the structure morphism of a $\Gamma$-comodule $M$ is written $\psi_M : M \rightarrow \Gamma \otimes_A M$.
nodes.section: A Cohomology and cocycles for Hopf algebroids

nodes.name: Flat Hopf algebroid hypothesis
nodes.statement: Throughout this section, $(A,\Gamma)$ is a flat Hopf algebroid, so that $\Gamma \hspace{-.2em}-\hspace{-.2em} \mathrm{Comod}$ is abelian with enough injectives; extension groups in this category are denoted by $\mathrm{Ext}_\Gamma$; the extended comodule functor $\Gamma \otimes _A - : A\hspace{-.2em}-\hspace{-.2em} \mathrm{Mod} \rightarrow \Gamma \hspace{-.2em}-\hspace{-.2em} \mathrm{Comod}$ is right adjoint to the forgetful functor $\Gamma \hspace{-.2em}-\hspace{-.2em} \mathrm{Comod} \rightarrow A \hspace{-.2em}-\hspace{-.2em} \mathrm{Mod}$.

nodes.name: Unreduced cobar resolution
nodes.statement: For $M$ a $\Gamma$-comodule, let $(\tilde{D}_\Gamma ^\bullet M, d^\bullet)$ denote the unreduced cobar resolution of $M$ (Cf. \cite[Definition A1.2.11]{ravenel_green}).

nodes.name: A-projective and relatively injective comodules
nodes.statement: \ \begin{enumerate} \item A $\Gamma$-comodule $X$ is $A$-projective if its underlying $A$-module is projective. \item A $\Gamma$-comodule $J$ is relatively injective if it has the morphism extension problem with respect to monomorphisms of $\Gamma$-comodules which are split as $A$-module morphisms. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Relatively injective comodules are summands of extended comodules
nodes.statement: A $\Gamma$-comodule $J$ is relatively injective if and only if it is a direct summand of an extended comodule.
conclusions: $J$ is relatively injective if and only if it is a direct summand of an extended comodule.
equivalent_conditions: it is a direct summand of an extended comodule

nodes.name: Ext into extended comodules
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a $\Gamma$-comodule and $N$ an $A$-module. Then there is a natural isomorphism \[ \mathrm{Ext}^i _\Gamma (M, \Gamma \otimes _A N ) \cong \mathrm{Ext}^i _A (M, N) . \] Hence, if $X$ is an $A$-projective $\Gamma$-comodule and $J$ is a relatively injective $\Gamma$-comodule, \[ \mathrm{Ext}^i _\Gamma(X, J) = \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{Hom}_\Gamma (X, J) & i= 0 \\ 0 & i >0. \end{array} \right. \]
assumptions: $M$ be a $\Gamma$-comodule and $N$ an $A$-module
$X$ is an $A$-projective $\Gamma$-comodule and $J$ is a relatively injective $\Gamma$-comodule
conclusions: there is a natural isomorphism \[ \mathrm{Ext}^i _\Gamma (M, \Gamma \otimes _A N ) \cong \mathrm{Ext}^i _A (M, N) . \]
\mathrm{Ext}^i _\Gamma(X, J) = \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{Hom}_\Gamma (X, J) & i= 0 \\ 0 & i >0. \end{array} \right. \]

assumptions: $M$ be a $\Gamma$-comodule and $N$ an $A$-module
conclusions: there is a natural isomorphism \[ \mathrm{Ext}^i _\Gamma (M, \Gamma \otimes _A N ) \cong \mathrm{Ext}^i _A (M, N) . \]

assumptions: $X$ is an $A$-projective $\Gamma$-comodule and $J$ is a relatively injective $\Gamma$-comodule
conclusions: \mathrm{Ext}^i _\Gamma(X, J) = \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{Hom}_\Gamma (X, J) & i= 0 \\ 0 & i >0. \end{array} \right. \]

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.3
nodes.statement: The result follows from the argument of \cite[Lemma A1.2.8b)]{ravenel_green}.
nodes.statement_short: Follow the argument of Ravenel, Lemma A1.2.8.

nodes.name: Ext computed by the cobar complex
nodes.statement: \cite[Lemma A.1.1.6, Corollary A1.2.12]{ravenel_green} Let $X$ be an $A$-projective $\Gamma$-comodule and $M$ be a $\Gamma$-comodule. Then $ \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet_\Gamma (X, M)$ can be calculated by a resolution of $M$ of the from $M \rightarrow J^\bullet$, where each $J^k$ is relatively injective. In particular, $ \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet_\Gamma (X, M)$ is naturally isomorphic to the cohomology of the cocomplex $\mathrm{Hom}_\Gamma (X, \tilde{D}^\bullet_\Gamma M)$, which has terms $\mathrm{Hom}_A (X, \Gamma^{\otimes_A s }\otimes _A M)$.
assumptions: $X$ be an $A$-projective $\Gamma$-comodule and $M$ be a $\Gamma$-comodule
conclusions: $ \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet_\Gamma (X, M)$ can be calculated by a resolution of $M$ of the from $M \rightarrow J^\bullet$, where each $J^k$ is relatively injective.

$ \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet_\Gamma (X, M)$ is naturally isomorphic to the cohomology of the cocomplex $\mathrm{Hom}_\Gamma (X, \tilde{D}^\bullet_\Gamma M)$, which has terms $\mathrm{Hom}_A (X, \Gamma^{\otimes_A s }\otimes _A M)$.
nodes.label: prop:ext-cobar

nodes.name: Ext^1 classes represented by 1-cocycles
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be an $A$-projective $\Gamma$-comodule and $M$ be a $\Gamma$-comodule. An extension class $[\kappa] \in \mathrm{Ext}^1 _\Gamma (X, M)$ is represented by a cocycle $\kappa \in \mathrm{Hom}_A (X, \Gamma \otimes_A M )$.
assumptions: $X$ be an $A$-projective $\Gamma$-comodule and $M$ be a $\Gamma$-comodule
conclusions: An extension class $[\kappa] \in \mathrm{Ext}^1 _\Gamma (X, M)$ is represented by a cocycle $\kappa \in \mathrm{Hom}_A (X, \Gamma \otimes_A M )$.

nodes.name: First cobar differential d^0
nodes.statement: Let $X, M$ be as in Proposition \ref{prop:ext-cobar} and let $\alpha : M \rightarrow N$ be a morphism of $\Gamma$-comodules. \begin{enumerate} \item The differential $d^0_M : \mathrm{Hom}_A (X, M) \rightarrow \mathrm{Hom}_A (X, \Gamma \otimes_A M )$ is given by $ d^0_M g := (\Gamma \otimes g ) \circ \psi_X - \psi_M \circ g. $ \item The differential $d^0_N : \mathrm{Hom}_A (X, N) \rightarrow \mathrm{Hom}_A (X, \Gamma \otimes_A N )$ satisfies the relation $ d^0_N (\alpha \circ g) = (\Gamma \otimes _A \alpha) \circ d^0_M g. $ \end{enumerate}

For a morphism of $\Gamma$-comodules $h : X \rightarrow N_3$ and any lift $\tilde{h}: X\rightarrow N_2$ of $h$ as a morphism of $A$-modules: \begin{enumerate} \item the morphism $\Delta \tilde{h}:= (\Gamma \otimes \tilde{h}) \circ \psi_X - \psi_{N_2} \circ \tilde{h}$ lies in the image of $\mathrm{Hom}_A (X, \Gamma \otimes_A N_1 ) \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Hom}_A (X, \Gamma \otimes_A N_2)$; \item the morphism $\Delta \tilde{h} : X \rightarrow \Gamma \otimes_A N_1$ is a cocycle and the associated class in $\mathrm{Ext}^1 _\Gamma (X, N_1)$ satisfies $[\Delta \tilde{h}] = \partial h$, where $\partial : \mathrm{Hom}_\Gamma (X, N_3) \rightarrow \mathrm{Ext}^1_\Gamma (X, N_1)$ is the connecting morphism. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Cocycle from a module splitting
nodes.statement: Let \begin{eqnarray} 0 \rightarrow M \rightarrow \mathcal{E} \stackrel{p}{\rightarrow} X \rightarrow 0 \end{eqnarray} be a short exact sequence of $\Gamma$-comodules, in which $X$ is $A$-projective. Then, for any choice of section $\sigma : X \rightarrow \mathcal{E}$, with associated retract $r :\mathcal{E}\rightarrow M$, the composite: \[ X \stackrel{- \sigma}{\rightarrow} \mathcal{E} \stackrel{\psi_{\mathcal{E}}}{\rightarrow} \Gamma \otimes _A \mathcal{E} \stackrel{\Gamma \otimes r}{\rightarrow} \Gamma \otimes_A M \] is a cocycle which represents the extension class $\partial 1_X$, which corresponds to the short exact sequence (\ref{eqn:ses-comod}). nodes.name: Proof of Proposition A.8
nodes.statement: Consider the cocycle given by Lemma \ref{lem:explicit-connecting}, where $h$ is taken to be the identity morphism of $X$ and $\tilde{h}$ the section $\sigma$. Then the morphism $\Delta \tilde{h}$ is the difference $(\Gamma \otimes \sigma) \circ \psi_X - \psi_{\mathcal{E}} \circ \sigma$, considered (by abuse of notation) also as a morphism to the image of $\Gamma \otimes_A M$ in $\Gamma \otimes_A \mathcal{E}$. Hence, composing with the retraction $\Gamma \otimes r$ gives $\Delta \tilde{h}=(\Gamma \otimes r) \Delta \tilde{h}$; now $r \circ \sigma =0$, so that $\Delta \tilde{h} = -( \Gamma \otimes r) \circ \psi _{\mathcal{E}} \circ \sigma$, as required. The final statement is clear.
